definition_zh: 合法地；依照法律地；从法律角度；（因符合法定条件而）在法律上
definition_en: in a way that is allowed or required by law, or as judged from the point of view of the law

senses.title: In a way the law allows
senses.definition: in a manner that is permitted by the law and not forbidden by it
senses.definitionCN: 以法律允许、未被法律禁止的方式
senses.example: Only after the clerk stamped the form could the shop legally hang its sign above the doorway.
senses.exampleCN: 只有在市政厅窗口盖章之后，店主才能合法地把招牌挂上门楣。
senses.why: Legal is the adjective of lex 'law', and the adverb -ly says the action matches that standard: what is done legally falls inside the permitted line.
senses.whyCN: legal 是 lex「法律」的形容词，副词词尾表示动作符合这一标准：合法地做的事落在许可线之内。

senses.title: As the law requires
senses.definition: in the way that a statute or regulation demands, whether or not one agrees with it
senses.definitionCN: 按法令或规章所要求的方式，无论个人是否赞同
senses.example: The landlord must legally give ninety days' notice before raising the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 房东涨租之前必须依法提前九十天通知。
senses.why: The same adverb covers permission and obligation, because a statute both permits and compels; the direction of the duty is read from context.
senses.whyCN: 同一个副词既覆盖许可也覆盖义务，因为法令既授权也强制；义务的方向靠上下文判断。

senses.title: Judged from the law's point of view
senses.definition: when assessed by the rules of law rather than by morality, custom or common sense
senses.definitionCN: 以法律规则而非道德、习俗或常识来评估
senses.example: Legally the contract is sound, though everyone agrees it was unfair.
senses.exampleCN: 从法律上看这份合同没有问题，尽管大家都认为它并不公平。
senses.why: Adverbs of viewpoint mark the frame being used, so legally at the head of a clause means 'in the legal frame, whatever other frames say'.
senses.whyCN: 表示视角的副词标出所用的框架，因此位于句首的 legally 意为「在法律框架内，不论其他框架怎么说」。

senses.title: With binding legal effect
senses.definition: so as to create rights and duties that a court would enforce
senses.definitionCN: 以至于产生法院会执行的的权利与义务
senses.example: Once notarised, the promise was legally binding on both families.
senses.exampleCN: 一经公证，这项承诺对两家都具有法律约束力。
senses.why: A document becomes real in law when the required form is completed, and the adverb names that completed state rather than the intention behind it.
senses.whyCN: 文件在形式上完成法定手续后，才在法律上生效；副词命名的是完成状态，而非背后的意图。

senses.title: By lawful procedure
senses.definition: through procedures and means that the law permits, especially in obtaining evidence or taking action
senses.definitionCN: 通过法律允许的程序与手段，尤指取得证据或采取行动
senses.example: The evidence was legally obtained, so the court admitted it.
senses.exampleCN: 证据是合法取得的，因此法院予以采纳。
senses.why: Procedure is where legality is tested in practice: a right result reached by a forbidden route is not legally reached.
senses.whyCN: 程序是合法性的实际检验处：用被禁止的途径得到的正确结果，在法律上不算取得。

senses.title: Meeting a statutory definition
senses.titleCN: 符合法定定义地（按法定标准）
senses.definition: according to a threshold or definition written into a statute, as with age or disability
senses.definitionCN: 按照写进法令的界限或定义，如年龄或残疾认定
senses.example: He is legally blind, though he still reads with a magnifier.
senses.exampleCN: 他在法律上属于失明，尽管他仍用放大镜读书。
senses.why: Statutes define words for their own purposes, so legally can mean 'by the official definition' even when ordinary usage would say otherwise.
senses.whyCN: 法令会为自己的目的给词下定义，因此 legally 可以表示「按官方定义」，即使日常说法并非如此。

senses.title: Recognised in legal status
senses.titleCN: 在法律上获得承认的（身份、关系）
senses.definition: in the status that the law recognises, as with a marriage or a registered charity
senses.definitionCN: 以法律所承认的身份，如婚姻或注册慈善机构
senses.example: They were legally married in a registry office, with two witnesses.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在登记处依法结婚，只有两位见证人。
senses.why: Status is conferred by registration, and the adverb separates the legal fact from any ceremony or private understanding.
senses.whyCN: 身份由登记赋予，副词把法律事实与任何仪式或私下理解区分开来。

senses.title: Qualified through legal training
senses.definition: by reason of professional legal training or qualification
senses.definitionCN: 凭借法律专业训练或执业资格
senses.example: She is legally trained but now writes about court reform.
senses.exampleCN: 她受过法律专业训练，如今撰写有关法院改革的文章。
senses.why: The adverb attaches to training as well as to acts, because a qualification is itself something the law recognises.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词也能附着于训练，因为资格本身就是法律所承认的东西。

intro.en: Legally is legal plus the adverb ending -ly. Legal comes from Latin legalis 'of the law', from lex 'law'; the deeper origin of lex itself is disputed.
intro.cn: legally 由 legal 加副词词尾构成。legal 来自拉丁 legalis「法律的」，出自 lex「法律」；而 lex 本身的更深来源存在争议。

items.en: Lex, genitive legis, meant a statute or a binding rule. It named the enacted rule, not the abstract idea of justice, which Latin kept for ius.
items.cn: lex（属格 legis）意为法令或有约束力的规则。它命名的是被制定的规则，而不是抽象的正义观念，后者在拉丁语中由 ius 承担。

items.en: Source uncertain (root of lex): lex is often connected with legere 'to read, to gather', but that link is a hypothesis; others derive it from a root meaning 'to lay down'. No single origin is established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（lex 的词根）：常有人把 lex 与 legere「读、收集」联系起来，但那只是假说；也有人把它追溯到表示「放置、立下」的词根。尚无单一结论。

items.en: Legalis 'of the law, lawful' was formed on the stem of lex and passed through French into English as legal in the medieval period.
items.cn: legalis「法律的、合法的」由 lex 的词干构成，经法语在中世纪进入英语，成为 legal。

items.en: The English adverb ending -ly, from Old English -lice, turns the adjective into a word describing how an act is done or from what angle it is judged.
items.cn: 英语的副词词尾源自古英语相应的词尾形式，把形容词变成描述「如何做」或「从哪个角度判断」的词。

items.en: As law became a profession, legally extended to training and qualification, not only to acts permitted by statute.
items.cn: 随着法律成为一门职业，legally 从「法令允许的行为」扩展到训练与资格。

items.en: The first dates for the adverb are approximate: legal is attested from the medieval period, while legally settles into its modern senses in the early modern centuries.
items.cn: 这个副词的最早年代为约数：legal 在中世纪已有书证，legally 则在近代早期逐渐定型为今天的各义。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin law word and differs only in shade; the second group names other kinds of conformity to rule.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个拉丁「法律」词，差别只在分寸；第二组是对规则的其他种类的符合。

entries.definition: The adjective: permitted by law, or belonging to law as a field.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：法律允许的，或属于法律领域的。

entries.definition: The quality of being lawful, or the question of whether something satisfies the law.
entries.definitionCN: 合乎法律的性质，或某事物是否满足法律要求的问题。

entries.definition: To change the law so that something previously forbidden becomes permitted.
entries.definitionCN: 修改法律，使原先被禁止的事变为允许。

entries.definition: Forbidden by law; the negative prefix reverses the permission without changing the root.
entries.definitionCN: 法律所禁止的；否定前缀把许可翻转为禁止，词根不变。

entries.definition: Concerned with making statutes, from lex plus latum 'carried'; it describes the making, not the obeying.
entries.definitionCN: 与制定法令有关，由 lex 加「携带」的过去分词构成；它描述制定，而非遵守。

entries.definition: In a way allowed by law, using the everyday noun law rather than the Latin one.
entries.definitionCN: 以法律允许的方式，用的是日常的 law 而非拉丁词。

entries.definition: In accordance with the constitution, which outranks an ordinary statute.
entries.definitionCN: 依宪法而行，效力高于普通法令。

entries.definition: By the terms of a particular statute, used mostly in official and legal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 按某部具体法令的条款，多用于官方与法律文书。

entries.definition: So as to have legal effect; a valid act may still be illegal if the wrong person performed it.
entries.definitionCN: 以至于具有法律效力；有效的行为若由无权者作出，仍可能违法。

entries.definition: By a just or rightful claim, which may or may not coincide with the statute book.
entries.definitionCN: 凭正当权利，可能与成文法令一致，也可能不一致。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin law word, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「法律」词、真实的同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Lex is Latin for law, and -ly turns the adjective into the manner: in the manner of the law.
normal.cn: lex 是拉丁语「法律」，副词词尾把形容词变成方式：以法律的方式。

normal.en: The family runs legal, legally, legality, legalise, legalisation and illegal.
normal.cn: 同族词有 legal、legally、legality、legalise、legalisation 与 illegal。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the binding sense: legally binding, legally required, legally entitled.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出约束力义：具有法律约束力、法律要求、依法有权。

normal.en: Latin kept ius for justice and lex for the statute, a split English later lost.
normal.cn: 拉丁语用 ius 表正义、用 lex 表法令，这一区分后来的英语丢掉了。

normal.en: A stamp on a form is the everyday picture of something becoming legally true.
normal.cn: 在表格上盖章，就是「某事在法律上成真」的日常画面。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens only when a seal is pressed onto the paper beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，只有把印章压在旁边的纸上，门才会开。

abstract.en: Picture two identical letters, one inside the envelope and one still on the desk, differing only by a date stamp.
abstract.cn: 想象两封一模一样的信，一封进了信封，一封还在桌上，只差一个日期戳。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid on a table to decide which of two nearly equal lengths counts.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上放着一把尺，用来判定两个几乎一样长的东西哪个算数。

examples.en: The company acted legally by publishing the audit in full.
examples.cn: 该公司完整公布审计报告，行为合法。

examples.en: Legally, the land belongs to the trust, not to the family.
examples.cn: 从法律上看，这块地属于信托基金，而不属于这个家庭。

examples.en: Anyone legally resident for five years may apply for citizenship.
examples.cn: 任何合法居住满五年的人都可以申请入籍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「legal（合法的）+ ly（地）」——以合法的方式 → 合法地

root: 拉丁 lex（属格 legis）「法令、规则」（更深词根存疑）→ legalis「法律的」→ 法语 → 英语 legal；加副词词尾构成 legally。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one stamp: the stamp permits an act, compels a notice, fixes the frame of judgment, gives a document force, certifies a procedure, meets a statutory threshold, confers a status and finally recognises a qualification.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一枚印章：印章许可一个行为、强制一项通知、设定判断的框架、赋予文件效力、认证一道程序、达到法定界限、授予一种身份，最后承认一项资格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one seal pressed on paper, after which the same paper can do entirely different things.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚印章压在纸上，同一张纸从此能做完全不同的事。

branches.en: TWO DIRECTIONS OF THE SEAL: what the statute allows and what it demands are the same line read outward and inward.
branches.cn: 印章的两个方向：法令允许什么与要求什么，是同一条线向外读与向内读。

branches.en: THE FRAME: the adverb can step outside any particular rule and simply say which lens is being used.
branches.cn: 框架：副词可以退到任何具体规则之外，只说明正在使用哪一副镜头。

branches.en: FORCE AND ROUTE: a document with the seal, and evidence gathered the right way, are power plus the path that earned it.
branches.cn: 效力与路径：盖了章的文件与按规矩取得的证据，是力量加上挣得它的那条路径。

branches.en: DEFINITION AND STATUS: a threshold in a statute and a registration in a register both make a legal fact.
branches.cn: 定义与身份：法令里的界限与登记册上的一笔，都在制造一项法律事实。

branches.en: THE QUALIFIED PERSON: training itself becomes something the law recognises.
branches.cn: 有资格的人：训练本身也成为法律所承认的东西。

intro.en: Legally is a Latin law root, an adjective ending and an English adverb ending stacked in order.
intro.cn: legally 是把拉丁「法律」词根、形容词词尾与英语副词词尾依次叠加的结果。

latinIntro.en: Latin lex, genitive legis, gives legal, legality, legislate and legitimate; the English -ly ending marks manner or viewpoint.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lex（属格 legis）衍生 legal、legality、legislate 与 legitimate；英语的副词词尾标记方式或视角。

items.example: The root names the enacted rule.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名被制定的规则。

items.example: It forms the adjective of law.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示法律的形容词。

items.example: The adjective holds both senses at once.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词同时承载两义。

items.example: It forms the noun of being lawful.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「合乎法律」这一性质的名词。

items.example: The abstract noun of the standard.
It forms the verb of change.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示改变的动词。

items.example: The verb names the change in the statute book.
items.exampleCN: 动词命名法令文本上的改变。

items.example: It turns the adjective into an adverb.
The adverb carries permission, obligation and viewpoint.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词兼具许可、义务与视角。

items.example: It negates the adjective in illegal.
items.exampleCN: 它在「非法的」中否定形容词。

definition_en: the making of laws by an authorized body, or the body of laws so made
core_image: 议事厅里逐条朗读、举手表决，散会后书记员把通过的条文装订成厚册
scene: 辩论持续到深夜，反对党仍要求把每一条都念完再表决。Parliament passed legislation that rewrites the funding formula.
sceneCN: 这里 legislation 指立法机关通过的法律（第 2 个义项：法规总称）；句意为议会通过了一项改写拨款公式的法律。

forms.label: 复数（指多部法律，多见于美式用法）

senses.title: The making of laws
senses.definition: the process or act of making laws through an authorized body
senses.definitionCN: 由有权机关制定法律的过程或行为
senses.example: Legislation took eighteen months and three committees.
senses.exampleCN: 立法花了十八个月、经过三个委员会。
senses.why: the Latin noun names the bringing of a law, an act rather than a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词本指「把法带来」，是行为而非物品。

senses.title: Laws collectively
senses.definition: the whole body of enacted laws on a subject or in a jurisdiction
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域或某一法域已颁行的全部法律
senses.example: Environmental legislation now covers the whole watershed.
senses.exampleCN: 环境法规如今覆盖整个流域。
senses.why: mass-noun use treats statutes as one substance, which is how policy talk usually needs them.
senses.whyCN: 不可数用法把诸多法令当作一种物质，政策讨论通常正需要这样。

senses.title: A single statute
senses.definition: one enacted law, countable especially in American usage
senses.definitionCN: 一部已颁行的法律，在美式用法中可数
senses.example: Two legislations were merged into one act.
senses.exampleCN: 两部法令被合并为一项法案。
senses.why: American usage makes the noun countable because each bill becomes a numbered law.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法把这个名词可数化，因为每项议案都会成为一部编号法律。

senses.title: The legislative process
senses.definition: the staged procedure of reading, amending and voting that a bill must pass
senses.definitionCN: 议案必须经过的宣读、修正与表决的分阶段程序
senses.example: The rules of legislation favour whoever controls the agenda.
senses.exampleCN: 立法程序偏向掌控议程的一方。
senses.why: procedure is the machinery behind the act, and English uses the same noun for both.
senses.whyCN: 程序是行为背后的机器，英语用同一个名词兼指两者。

senses.title: What a legislature enacts
senses.definition: the output of a parliament or congress, as distinct from rules made by agencies
senses.definitionCN: 议会或国会的产出，区别于行政机关自订的规则
senses.example: Primary legislation needs a vote; guidance does not.
senses.exampleCN: 主要立法需要表决，行政指引则不必。
senses.why: the word marks the source of authority, so it separates parliamentary output from administrative rules.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标示权威来源，因此把议会产出与行政规则分开。

senses.title: Delegated legislation
senses.definition: rules made by a minister or agency under powers granted by a statute
senses.definitionCN: 部长或机关依法律授予的权力制定的规则
senses.example: Delegated legislation fills in technical detail the chamber cannot debate.
senses.exampleCN: 次级立法填补议会无法逐条辩论的技术细节。
senses.why: the word travels with the authority to make law, even when that authority has been lent out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词随立法权一同转移，即使该权力是被借出去的。

senses.title: Proposed legislation
senses.definition: a bill or draft still before the chamber, spoken of as future law
senses.definitionCN: 仍在议会审议、被视作未来法律的议案或草案
senses.example: Proposed legislation would cap the fee at ten percent.
senses.exampleCN: 拟议立法将把这个费用上限设为百分之十。
senses.why: the word is applied ahead of enactment because the shape of the law is already visible in the draft.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在通过之前就被使用，因为法律的形状在草案里已经可见。

senses.title: Rules for an organization
senses.titleCN: 引申：组织内部规则体系
senses.definition: the formal rules by which a body governs its own members or processes
senses.definitionCN: 某机构管理自身成员或流程的成文规则
senses.example: The society's legislation on conflicts of interest is three pages long.
senses.exampleCN: 该学会关于利益冲突的规则有三页纸。
senses.why: private bodies borrow the word when their rules begin to function like statutes.
senses.whyCN: 私人机构在其规则开始像法令一样运作时，便借用了这个词。

intro.en: Legislation comes from Latin legis latio 'a bringing of a law', from lex 'law' and latio 'a bringing', the noun of latus, the past participle of ferre 'to carry'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: legislation 来自拉丁 legis latio「把法带来」，由 lex「法」与 latio「带来」构成，后者是 ferre「搬运」的过去分词 latus 的名词形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lex meant 'law, statute, a motion put to the people'. Its deeper origin is not established; the old link to legere 'to read' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: lex 意为「法、法令、提交民众的动议」。其更深来源未得到证明；与 legere「读」的旧联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ferre 'to carry, bring' has the suppletive participle latus, from which latio 'a bringing' is formed; the two verbs were already fused in classical usage.
items.cn: ferre「搬运、带来」的过去分词为异干互补的 latus，由其构成 latio「带来」；两者在古典用法中已合并。

items.en: The phrase legis latio named the bringing of a bill before the assembly, a procedural act rather than the text itself.
items.cn: legis latio 这一说法指把议案带到大会之前的程序性行为，而非文本本身。

items.en: Medieval Latin legislatio generalized the phrase into the making of laws by any authorized body.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 legislatio 把这一说法一般化，指任何有权机关制定法律。

items.en: French législation passed into English in the seventeenth century, first as the act and soon after as the body of laws.
items.cn: 法语 législation 在 17 世纪进入英语，先指立法行为，不久也指法律总体。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is not precisely dated, and the origin of lex itself remains unsettled, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早的英语书证没有确切年代；lex 本身的来源仍无定论，为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the lex or legisl- stem; group two holds words for laws and for the making of them.
note.cn: 第一组共享 lex 或 legisl- 词干；第二组是关于法律与制定法律的词。

entries.definition: Describing a body or power that makes law; it cannot stand for the laws themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 描述制定法律的机关或权力；不能指法律本身。

entries.definition: The assembly that makes law, formed with -ure 'place or body'; a different thing from the laws it makes.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的议会，由 -ure「场所、机构」构成；与其所制定的法律是两回事。

entries.definition: One member who makes law; the noun names a role, not an output.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的成员之一；指角色，而非产出。

entries.definition: From Latin legitimus 'lawful', built on lex but through a different adjective; it means lawful, not law-making.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 legitimus「合法的」，虽出 lex 却经另一形容词；意为合法，而非立法。

entries.definition: A single rule or the whole body of rules; legislation is the making of it or the output as a mass.
entries.definitionCN: 单条规则或全部规则；legislation 指制定过程或作为总体的产出。

entries.definition: A single law passed by a legislature, countable and technical; legislation is the wider mass noun.
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关通过的单项法律，可数且技术化；legislation 是更宽的总称。

entries.definition: Detailed rules issued by an agency under a statute, usually not requiring a parliamentary vote.
entries.definitionCN: 机关依法令发布的细则，通常不经议会表决。

entries.definition: A draft law still under consideration; legislation names what it becomes, or the process of making it.
entries.definitionCN: 仍在审议的草案；legislation 指它最终成为的东西，或制定它的过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: legis latio: the bringing of a law, so the word began as a motion carried forward.
normal.cn: legis latio：把法带来，因此这个词本是一项被送上前的动议。

normal.en: The family runs legislate, legislation, legislative, legislator, legislature.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 legislate、legislation、legislative、legislator、legislature。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split act from output: pass legislation, delegated legislation, environmental legislation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出行为与产出：通过立法、授权立法、环境立法。

normal.en: Contrast the pair: a bill is the draft, legislation is the making and the mass of laws.
normal.cn: 对照这一对：bill 是草案，legislation 是制定过程与法律总体。

normal.en: Watch the false friend legitimate: lawful, but built on a different adjective of lex.
normal.cn: 提防假朋友 legitimate：意为合法，却由 lex 的另一形容词构成。

abstract.en: Picture a text carried by hand across a hall before anyone votes on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文本在被人手捧着穿过大厅，之后才有人表决。

abstract.en: Picture shelves that grow a new thick volume every session.
abstract.cn: 想象书架每开一次会就多一本厚册。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that must be read aloud before it can bind anyone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规则必须先被大声读出，才能约束任何人。

examples.en: The state's legislation on groundwater is older than its mapping.
examples.cn: 该州关于地下水的立法比水文测绘还要早。

examples.en: Delegated legislation filled in the standards the chamber left blank.
examples.cn: 次级立法填上了议会留白的技术标准。

examples.en: Industry lobbied against the proposed legislation for two years.
examples.cn: 业界游说反对这项拟议立法达两年。

dict_mnemonic.text: legis（法）+ lation（带来）＝ 把法带到台面上；记「念一遍、改一遍、举一次手」。

root: 拉丁 legis latio「把法带来」= lex「法」（更深来源不确定，与 legere「读」的联系仅为假说）+ latio「带来」（来自 ferre「搬运」的过去分词 latus）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a bill from act to archive: making law, the mass of law, one statute, the procedure, parliamentary output, delegated rules, drafts not yet passed, and the rules of a private body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项随一项议案从行为走到档案：立法、法律总体、单部法律、程序、议会产出、授权规则、尚未通过的草案，以及私人机构的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a text read aloud, amended, voted on, then bound into a thick volume.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份文本被朗读、修正、表决，最后装订进厚册。

branches.en: ACT AND MASS: the making of law, then the whole body it accumulates into.
branches.cn: 行为与总体：先制定，再累积成整体。

branches.en: ONE VOLUME: the countable unit inside the mass.
branches.cn: 单册：总体之中的可数单位。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: procedure at work, and the authority that makes its output law.
branches.cn: 机器：程序在运转，以及使其产成为法律的权威。

branches.en: LENT POWER: rule-making handed to ministers and agencies.
branches.cn: 借出的权力：规则制定权交到部长与机关手里。

branches.en: BEFORE AND AFTER THE HALL: drafts spoken of as law, and private bodies drafting their own.
branches.cn: 大厅前后：草案已被当作法律谈论，私人机构也自订规则。

intro.en: Legislation joins a Latin noun for law to a Latin noun for bringing, and the second element still appears in English words of transfer.
intro.cn: legislation 把拉丁语「法」的名词与「带来」的名词接在一起，后一成分仍出现在英语的转移类词中。

latinIntro.en: Lex supplies legal, legitimate and legislate; latus and ferre supply transfer, refer and relate.
latinIntro.cn: lex 衍生 legal、legitimate、legislate；latus 与 ferre 衍生 transfer、refer、relate。

items.example: Lex is the root of legal and legislate.
items.exampleCN: lex 是 legal 与 legislate 的词根。

items.example: Its participle latus hides inside latio.
items.exampleCN: 其分词 latus 藏在 latio 里。

items.example: Legis latio is the bringing of a bill.
items.exampleCN: legis latio 就是把议案带来。

items.example: The chamber legislates twice a year.
Legislation followed the report by a year.
items.exampleCN: 报告之后一年才有了立法。

items.example: The legislator read the amendment aloud.
items.exampleCN: 立法者大声读了修正案。

items.example: A legitimate claim differs from a popular one.
items.exampleCN: 合法的诉求与受欢迎的诉求不同。

definition_zh: 闲暇；空闲时间；休闲活动；悠闲；休闲（作定语）
definition_en: time free from work or duties, the activities that fill it, and the relaxed manner that such time allows
core_image: 安静午后的一张空藤椅，旁边放着一杯还冒着热气的茶
scene: 周末的午后，会议与邮件都停了，阳台上的藤椅空着，等一个人端着茶坐下来。Long afternoons of leisure left him free to read whatever he liked.
sceneCN: 这里是「空闲时间」（第 1 个义项：不必工作的自由时间）；句意为漫长的闲暇午后让他能随心读书。图中可辨识物件：阳台藤椅、茶杯、翻开的书。

pos.zh: 闲暇；空闲时间；休闲活动

derivatives.zh: 由 leisure 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「从容的；不慌不忙的」
由 leisure 加 -ed 构成，义为「有大量空闲时间的」
由 leisure 与 wear 复合而成，义为「休闲服饰」

senses.title: Time free from work or duty
senses.definition: time when you are not working and may choose for yourself what to do
senses.definitionCN: 不必工作、可以由自己决定做什么的那段时间
senses.example: She has little leisure during the exam season.
senses.exampleCN: 考试季她几乎没有空闲时间。
senses.why: Latin licere meant to be permitted, so leisure began as permitted time, the hours no duty can claim.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 licere 意为「被允许」，leisure 最初指被允许自由支配的时间，也就是没有职责占用的那几个小时。

senses.title: Activities enjoyed in that free time
senses.definition: the things people choose to do for pleasure when work is finished
senses.definitionCN: 工作结束后人们为了愉快而选择去做的事情
senses.example: Reading and cycling are his favourite forms of leisure.
senses.exampleCN: 读书和骑车是他最喜欢的休闲方式。
senses.why: Once free hours exist they must be filled, so the word slides from the empty time to the chosen activity that occupies it.
senses.whyCN: 空闲的小时一旦存在，就必然被填满，于是词义从「空白的时间」滑向占用这段时间的自选活动。

senses.title: An unhurried, easy manner
senses.definition: a relaxed way of acting, with no pressure of time and no need to rush
senses.definitionCN: 不受时间压迫、不必赶的轻松做事方式
senses.example: He answered the questions at his leisure.
senses.exampleCN: 他不慌不忙地回答了问题。
senses.why: Time that carries no deadline produces a manner without hurry, so at leisure comes to describe the calm inside the free hours.
senses.whyCN: 没有截止期限的时间会带来不赶的态度，于是 at leisure 用来描述空闲时间里那种从容的心境。

senses.title: Placed before a noun: made for free time
senses.definition: used in front of another noun for places, clothes or industries serving people at leisure
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一个名词前，指服务于闲暇之人的场所、衣物或产业
senses.example: The town opened a new leisure centre last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇去年春天新开了一家休闲中心。
senses.why: A noun naming free time easily turns into a label on the things built for it, which is why leisure attaches to centres, wear and whole industries.
senses.whyCN: 表示空闲时间的名词很容易变成「为其建造之物」的标签，所以 leisure 能贴在中心、服饰乃至整个产业前面。

intro.en: Leisure comes from a Latin verb of permission and reached English through French, still carrying the idea of hours that nobody else can claim.
intro.cn: leisure 源自拉丁语中表示「允许」的动词，经法语进入英语，至今仍带着「无人能占用的时间」这层意思。

items.en: Licere meant to be allowed or permitted, and it named what a person was free to do.
items.cn: licere 意为「被允许、获准」，指一个人可以自由去做的事。

items.en: Its noun licentia named permission or freedom, the state of being allowed.
items.cn: 其名词 licentia 表示许可或自由，即「获准的状态」。

items.en: Old French shaped the verb as leisir, which meant both to be allowed and the free time that followed.
items.cn: 古法语把动词写作 leisir，既表示「被允许」，也指随之而来的空闲时间。

items.en: Middle English used leisir, later spelled leisure, for time at one's own disposal.
items.cn: 中古英语用 leisir（后写作 leisure）指由自己支配的时间。

items.en: Modern English keeps leisure for free time and extends it to leisure activities, leisure wear and the leisure industry.
items.cn: 现代英语用 leisure 指空闲时间，并扩展到休闲活动、休闲服饰与休闲产业。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same Latin verb of permission; the near-meaning group collects words for spare hours and rest.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「允许」动词上的派生形式；近义组收表示空闲与休息的词。

entries.definition: Acting or moving without hurry.
entries.definitionCN: 不慌不忙的；从容的。

entries.definition: Having plenty of free time, usually through wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 有大量空闲时间的，通常因富裕。

entries.definition: Allowed by law; the opposite of illicit.
entries.definitionCN: 法律允许的；illicit 的反义词。

entries.definition: Official permission to do something, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 官方许可，来自同一拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Time left over after work or duties.
entries.definitionCN: 工作或职责之外剩下的时间。

entries.definition: Resting and letting tension go.
entries.definitionCN: 休息，让紧张消退。

entries.definition: Activities done for enjoyment outside work.
entries.definitionCN: 工作之外为消遣而做的活动。

entries.definition: The state of not working, often with a hint of disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 不做事的状态，常带一点贬义。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb for being allowed, and its family keeps returning to permission, free hours and the easy manner they produce.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「获准」的拉丁动词上，同族词反复回到许可、空闲时间以及由此产生的从容态度。

normal.en: Licere in Latin means to be allowed, so leisure is time you are permitted to spend as you wish.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 licere 意为被允许，所以 leisure 是可以随自己支配的获准时间。

normal.en: Old French leisir dropped its verb ending and became leisure, keeping both the permission and the free hours.
normal.cn: 古法语 leisir 去掉动词词尾后成为 leisure，同时保留「许可」和「空闲时间」两层意思。

normal.en: Leisurely adds -ly to leisure, describing the unhurried manner of someone inside free time.
normal.cn: leisurely 在 leisure 后加 -ly，形容人处在空闲时间里的从容样子。

normal.en: Leisure wear joins leisure to wear, clothing for hours when no uniform is required.
normal.cn: leisure wear 把 leisure 与 wear 连起来，指不必穿制服的时段所穿的衣服。

normal.en: The phrase is at leisure, not in leisure, because you sit inside your own free time.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 at leisure 而不是 in leisure，因为人坐在自己的空闲时间里。

abstract.en: A word that first meant permission reminds us that free time is not empty space but time granted to us.
abstract.cn: 一个最初表示「许可」的词提醒人：空闲不是空白，而是被准许使用的时光。

abstract.en: Leisure links restful hours with a calm manner, suggesting that how we spend time shapes how we carry ourselves.
abstract.cn: leisure 把休息的时段与从容的态度连在一起，说明怎样花时间会影响人的举止。

abstract.en: When leisure becomes an industry, the very hours once free now have goods built around them.
abstract.cn: 当 leisure 变成一种产业，原本自由的时段周围就长出了专门为它制造的商品。

examples.en: She has little leisure during the exam season.
examples.cn: 考试季她几乎没有空闲时间。

examples.en: Reading and cycling are his favourite forms of leisure.
examples.cn: 读书和骑车是他最喜欢的休闲方式。

examples.en: He answered the questions at his leisure.
examples.cn: 他不慌不忙地回答了问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来这儿」——有空的时候，来这儿坐坐；记住 leisure 是空闲、闲暇。

root: 拉丁语 licere（被允许）→ 拉丁名词 licentia（许可）→ 古法语 leisir（获准的空闲）→ 中古英语 leisure；同族词多与「许可、自由」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is permitted free time; from it grow the activities that fill those hours, the unhurried manner they allow, and the attributive use for things made for them.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「被允许自由支配的时间」；由此长出填充这些时间的活动、随之而来的从容态度，以及修饰休闲事物的定语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty chair on a quiet afternoon, waiting for someone with nowhere else to be.
core.cn: 核心意象：安静午后的一张空椅子，等一个无别处可去的人。

branches.en: a clock with no appointment marked on it
branches.cn: 一只没有记下任何约会的钟

branches.en: a bicycle leaning against a park bench
branches.cn: 靠在公园长椅上的自行车

branches.en: a town building named after free hours
branches.cn: 以闲暇时光命名的小镇建筑

branches.en: a man answering slowly, with no deadline
branches.cn: 不赶时间、从容作答的人

branches.en: a shop window full of clothes for weekends
branches.cn: 橱窗里摆满周末穿的休闲衣

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb of permission and its noun, reshaped by French, then extended by English suffixes into a manner and a garment.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示许可的拉丁动词及其名词支撑，经法语改写，再由英语后缀扩展出「态度」和「衣物」。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 柠檬；柠檬树；柠檬黄；次品
definition_en: a sour yellow citrus fruit, the tree that bears it, its pale colour, and an informal word for something badly made
core_image: 白盘里一只切开的黄色果子，酸气比汁水先到
scene: 早餐桌上，一只切开的果子躺在白盘里，酸味先钻进鼻子，旁边一杯清水还没加糖。She cut the lemon in half and squeezed it over the fish.
sceneCN: 这里是「柠檬」（第 1 个义项：那种黄色酸果）；句意是她把柠檬切成两半，挤在鱼上。图中可辨识物件：白盘、切开的黄色果子、玻璃水杯。

pos.zh: 柠檬；柠檬树；柠檬黄；次品

derivatives.zh: 由 lemon 加饮料后缀 -ade 构成，义为「柠檬水；柠檬饮料」
由 lemon 加 -y 构成，义为「有柠檬味或柠檬色的」
由 lemon 与 grass 复合而成，义为「柠檬草」

senses.title: The yellow citrus fruit
senses.definition: a yellow citrus fruit with a very sour juice and a thick peel
senses.definitionCN: 一种黄色的柑橘果实，汁水极酸，果皮厚
senses.example: She cut the lemon in half and squeezed it over the fish.
senses.exampleCN: 她把柠檬切成两半，挤在鱼上。
senses.why: The fruit is the first thing the borrowed word names, and every other sense in English grows out of its colour, its tree and its sourness.
senses.whyCN: 这个借词最初指的正是这种果子，英语里其余义项都从它的颜色、树木与酸味衍生出来。

senses.title: The tree that bears it
senses.definition: the small evergreen tree on which lemons grow
senses.definitionCN: 结出柠檬的那种小型常绿乔木
senses.example: The lemon tree in the yard flowered early this year.
senses.exampleCN: 院子里的柠檬树今年开花早。
senses.why: Fruit names in English commonly spread to the plant that produces them, so the word names the tree as well as its crop.
senses.whyCN: 英语中果实名称常扩展到结出果实的植物，于是这个词既指果子，也指树。

senses.title: A pale bright yellow colour
senses.definition: a light, clear yellow like the skin of the fruit
senses.definitionCN: 像果皮那样的浅而明亮的黄色
senses.example: She painted the kitchen wall lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 她把厨房的墙刷成了柠檬黄。
senses.why: Because the peel is a strong clear yellow, the fruit itself becomes a colour sample that other things are measured against.
senses.whyCN: 因为果皮是鲜亮的黄色，果子本身就成了比色的样本，别的东西都拿它来对照。

senses.title: Something badly made, especially a car
senses.titleCN: 次品；中看不中用的东西
senses.definition: an informal word for a product, especially a vehicle, that keeps failing after you buy it
senses.definitionCN: 口语说法，指买回家后毛病不断的产品，尤指汽车
senses.example: He bought a used car that turned out to be a lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 他买的那辆二手车结果是个次品。
senses.why: Why a sour fruit should mean a bad purchase is not certain; one common explanation is that such goods taste sour to the buyer, like an unripe lemon.
senses.whyCN: 酸果子为什么能指「买错的东西」并无定论，一种常见解释是这种货对买主来说像未熟的柠檬一样酸。

intro.en: Lemon travelled west along trade routes, from a South Asian word for citrus through Persian and Arabic into French; its ultimate starting point is still debated.
intro.cn: lemon 沿着贸易路线西传，从南亚表示柑橘的词经波斯语、阿拉伯语进入法语，它更早的起点至今仍有争议。

items.en: A form like nimbu named a citrus fruit, and many dictionaries treat it as the most likely starting point, though this is not certain.
items.cn: 类似 nimbu 的形式指一种柑橘，多数词典把它当作最可能的起点，但这并不确定。

items.en: Persian limun named the fruit and passed the word to traders further west.
items.cn: 波斯语 limun 指这种果子，并把词传给更西边的商人。

items.en: Arabic laymun covered lemons and similar citrus and carried the word across the Mediterranean.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 laymun 泛指柠檬与类似柑橘，并把这个词带过地中海。

items.en: Old French limon named the fruit, and English borrowed it in the medieval period.
items.cn: 古法语 limon 指这种果子，英语在中世纪把它借了过来。

items.en: Modern English keeps lemon for the fruit and adds a colour name plus an informal sense for a defective purchase.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lemon 指果实，又添上颜色名，以及指「买到次品」的口语义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built from the borrowed fruit name and one close spelling with a separate history; the near-meaning group collects other citrus fruit and the taste they share.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个借来的果名构成的词，以及一个拼写接近但来源不同的词；近义组收其他柑橘果实与它们共有的味道。

entries.definition: A sweet drink made with lemon juice.
entries.definitionCN: 用柠檬汁加糖做的饮料。

entries.definition: Tasting or smelling of lemon.
entries.definitionCN: 有柠檬味道或气味的。

entries.definition: The French and Spanish spelling of the same borrowed word.
entries.definitionCN: 法语与西班牙语中同一借词的拼写。

entries.definition: A green citrus fruit; the spelling is close but the history is separate.
entries.definitionCN: 一种绿色柑橘；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The family of fruits that includes lemons and oranges.
entries.definitionCN: 包括柠檬与橙子在内的柑橘类。

entries.definition: A large citrus fruit with a bitter-sour taste.
entries.definitionCN: 一种大个头、苦酸的柑橘。

entries.definition: A round citrus fruit with sweet juice.
entries.definitionCN: 圆形、汁甜的柑橘。

entries.definition: Having a sharp taste like lemon juice.
entries.definitionCN: 像柠檬汁那样尖锐的酸味。

normalIntro.en: The word arrived by trade route rather than through Latin grammar, so its parts are the borrowed forms themselves plus English endings that build drinks, flavours and compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是沿贸易路线传进来的，不是靠拉丁语法拼合的，所以它的构件就是那些借词形式，再加上造饮料、造味道、造复合词的英语词尾。

normal.en: The word came west with the fruit, so the sequence Persian limun, Arabic laymun, French limon is the spine of the history.
normal.cn: 这个词跟着果子一起西传，波斯语 limun、阿拉伯语 laymun、法语 limon 这条线就是它的历史主干。

normal.en: Lemonade adds -ade, a suffix for drinks made from a fruit, so the spelling keeps the fruit whole and bolts on the drink.
normal.cn: lemonade 加了表示「果汁饮料」的后缀 -ade，拼写保留整个果名，再接上饮料义。

normal.en: Lemony adds -y to lemon, meaning having the taste or smell of the fruit.
normal.cn: lemony 在 lemon 后加 -y，表示「带有这种果子的味道或气味」。

normal.en: Lemongrass is a compound: a grass that smells like lemon but is not the fruit at all.
normal.cn: lemongrass 是复合词：一种闻起来像柠檬的草，和果子完全不是一回事。

normal.en: Lemon yellow works as a colour word because the peel gives a fixed sample that paint can be matched to.
normal.cn: lemon yellow 能当颜色词，是因为果皮提供了一个固定的比色样本。

abstract.en: One borrowed fruit name multiplies into a tree, a colour and a warning about bad purchases, which shows how far a concrete thing can travel.
abstract.cn: 一个借来的果名能长成树、长成颜色，还长成一句「买到次品」的警告，可见具体之物能走多远。

abstract.en: The sourness that makes the fruit useful in cooking is also what makes it a natural image for disappointment.
abstract.cn: 让果实在厨房里好用的那股酸，也正是它适合比喻失望的原因。

abstract.en: A word carried along trade routes reminds us that language often travels with goods, not with armies or grammars.
abstract.cn: 一个沿贸易路线传来的词提醒人：语言常常跟着货物走，而不是跟着军队或语法书走。

examples.en: She cut the lemon in half and squeezed it over the fish.
examples.cn: 她把柠檬切成两半，挤在鱼上。

examples.en: The lemon tree in the yard flowered early this year.
examples.cn: 院子里的柠檬树今年开花早。

examples.en: He bought a used car that turned out to be a lemon.
examples.cn: 他买的那辆二手车结果是个次品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「柠檬」正是 lemon 的音译——汉语这个词本来就借自英文，读音几乎一样。

root: 经波斯语 limun、阿拉伯语 laymun、古法语 limon 进入英语；更早的起点一般认为是梵语中表示柑橘的 nimbu，但来源仍有争议，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the sour yellow fruit; the senses then name the tree it grows on, the colour of its peel, and a defective purchase that leaves a sour taste.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是酸味的黄色果实；义项由此分出结出它的树、果皮的颜色，以及让人心里发酸的次品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a halved yellow fruit on a white plate, its sourness reaching the nose before the first bite.
core.cn: 核心意象：白盘里一只切开的黄果，酸气在第一口之前就先冲到鼻子里。

branches.en: a halved fruit dripping onto grilled fish
branches.cn: 切半的果子把汁滴在烤鱼上

branches.en: a small tree with glossy leaves in a yard
branches.cn: 院子里一株叶片油亮的小树

branches.en: a kitchen wall painted the colour of peel
branches.cn: 一面刷成果皮色的厨房墙

branches.en: a tray of cold drinks at a summer stall
branches.cn: 夏日小摊上的一盘冷饮

branches.en: a buyer kicking the tyre of a bad car
branches.cn: 买主踢着破车的轮胎

intro.en: Because the word entered English by trade rather than by derivation, its parts are the borrowed forms themselves plus English endings that build a drink, a flavour and a pair of compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词是经贸易而非构词进入英语的，所以它的构件就是那些借词形式，再加上造饮料、造味道、造两个复合词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Lemon came through Arabic and French rather than Latin, so no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: lemon 是经阿拉伯语与法语进来的，并非源自拉丁语，因此没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 借出；出借；放贷；提供（帮助）；适宜于
definition_en: to give something to someone for a time, to supply money on credit, and to hand over help, attention or a quality
core_image: 一只手把伞递出去，另一只手空着，等伞回来
scene: 雨天教室门口，一个人把伞递过去，自己缩起肩膀跑进雨里。He lent her his umbrella and walked home wet.
sceneCN: 这里是「借出」（第 1 个义项：把东西暂时交给别人用）；句意是他把伞借给她，自己淋着雨回家。图中可辨识物件：雨伞、雨滴、教室门框。

pos.zh: 借出；出借；放贷；提供；适宜于

derivatives.zh: 由 lend 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「出借人；放贷方」
由 lend 加 -ing 构成，义为「出借；放贷业务」
由 lend 加 -able 构成，义为「可出借的」

senses.title: To give something for a limited time
senses.titleCN: 借出（把东西暂时给别人用）
senses.definition: to give an object to someone on the understanding that it will come back later
senses.definitionCN: 把某物交给别人，双方都明白以后要归还
senses.example: He lent her his umbrella and walked home wet.
senses.exampleCN: 他把伞借给她，自己淋着雨回家。
senses.why: The old verb means granting the use of a thing rather than giving it away, so the object is expected to return and the owner keeps it.
senses.whyCN: 这个古词本义是「准许别人使用」，而不是「送出去」，所以东西预期会回来，主人始终保有它。

senses.title: To supply money that must be repaid
senses.definition: to give money to a person or business for a period, usually with interest
senses.definitionCN: 把钱在一段时间内交给个人或企业，通常收取利息
senses.example: The bank lends money to small firms at a fixed rate.
senses.exampleCN: 银行按固定利率向小公司放贷。
senses.why: Money is the thing most often granted for a period, so the general verb of temporary giving becomes the standard word for credit.
senses.whyCN: 钱是最常被「限期交付」的东西，于是这个表示暂时给予的通用动词成了「信贷」的标准说法。

senses.title: To be suitable for a particular use
senses.definition: to have qualities that make something easy or fitting to do
senses.definitionCN: 具备某些性质，使某件事做起来合适或容易
senses.example: The quiet garden lends itself to long conversations.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的花园很适合长谈。
senses.why: English says a place lends itself to a purpose, as if it handed its own qualities over for a while, which is why suitability comes out of the lending image.
senses.whyCN: 英语说某地「把自己借给」某种用途，仿佛它把自己的性质暂时交出来，所以「适合」这层意思是从借出的形象里长出来的。

senses.title: To offer help, attention or support
senses.definition: to give help, an ear or support to someone for as long as it is needed
senses.definitionCN: 在别人需要时给予帮助、倾听或支持
senses.example: She lent an ear to every student who needed one.
senses.exampleCN: 凡是需要倾诉的学生，她都愿意听。
senses.why: Help and attention can be handed over for a while without being owned, so the same verb covers listening, backing and encouragement.
senses.whyCN: 帮助与关注可以暂时交付而不必归对方所有，所以同一个动词也能覆盖倾听、支持与鼓励。

intro.en: Lend is a native Germanic verb, twin to the noun loan, and its irregular past lent keeps an old English shape.
intro.cn: lend 是土生土长的日耳曼语动词，与名词 loan 同出一源，不规则过去式 lent 保留了古英语的形态。

items.en: A reconstructed root laihwan meant to lend, or to leave something with someone for a time.
items.cn: 重构词根 laihwan 意为借出，或把东西暂时留在别人手里。

items.en: Old English lǣnan meant to grant the use of something, and the related noun lǣn meant a loan.
items.cn: 古英语 lǣnan 意为准许别人使用某物，相关名词 lǣn 意为借出物。

items.en: Norse speakers used a related verb, and their forms reinforced the English word in the north of England.
items.cn: 北欧使用者有相关动词，其形式在英格兰北部强化了英语这个词。

items.en: Middle English lenen kept the short past form lent, which survived into modern use.
items.cn: 中古英语 lenen 保留了短过去式 lent，并一直沿用到现代。

items.en: Modern English keeps lend as the verb and loan as the noun, with lent serving as both past tense and past participle.
items.cn: 现代英语让 lend 固定为动词、loan 作名词，lent 同时充当过去式与过去分词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun twin and two forms built with English suffixes; the near-meaning group collects words for borrowing, credit and money advanced.
note.cn: 形近组收同源名词与两个用英语后缀构成的派生形式；近义组收表示借入、信贷与垫付的词。

entries.definition: The noun twin of lend, naming the thing or sum that is lent.
entries.definitionCN: lend 的同源名词，指被借出的东西或款项。

entries.definition: A person or bank that lends.
entries.definitionCN: 出借人或放贷机构。

entries.definition: The act or business of lending money.
entries.definitionCN: 出借行为；放贷业务。

entries.definition: To take something for a time and agree to return it.
entries.definitionCN: 暂时拿走某物并同意归还，方向与 lend 相反。

entries.definition: To pay money before it is due, or to lend it.
entries.definitionCN: 提前支付或在到期前垫付。

entries.definition: Permission to pay later for goods or money received.
entries.definitionCN: 先收货或收款、以后付款的许可。

entries.definition: To give something formally, often a right or a favour.
entries.definitionCN: 正式给予，多指权利或恩惠。

normalIntro.en: The word is a native Germanic verb whose noun twin is loan, and its family keeps returning to temporary giving and the trust that makes it possible.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是土生土长的日耳曼语动词，同源名词是 loan，同族词反复回到「暂时给予」以及让这种给予成为可能的信任。

normal.en: Lend and loan are twins from the same root: the verb lends, the noun is the loan.
normal.cn: lend 与 loan 同出一源：动词是 lend，借出的东西是 loan。

normal.en: The past tense is lent, not lended, because the old strong shape survived while most verbs became regular.
normal.cn: 过去式是 lent 而不是 lended，因为古老的强变化形态留了下来，而多数动词都变成了规则变化。

normal.en: Lender adds -er to lend: the person or bank on the giving side.
normal.cn: lender 在 lend 后加 -er，指出借的一方，可以是人，也可以是银行。

normal.en: Lending adds -ing and turns the act into a business, as in bank lending.
normal.cn: lending 加 -ing，把行为变成一门业务，如银行放贷。

normal.en: Lend itself to is fixed: the thing lends itself, never lends to itself, when it suits a use.
normal.cn: 固定说法是 lend itself to：表示适合某种用途时，用反身形式，不能省掉 itself。

abstract.en: A word for handing something over temporarily is also a word for trust, since every loan assumes the other person will return it.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「暂时交出」的词同时也是「信任」的词，因为每一次出借都预设对方会归还。

abstract.en: Lending a hand and lending money share one verb, which quietly ranks money and help as similar kinds of gift.
abstract.cn: 借出一只手和借出钱共用一个动词，这悄悄把钱与帮助归为同一类给予。

abstract.en: The fact that a garden can lend itself to talk shows how English turns an act of giving into a statement about fitness.
abstract.cn: 花园能「把自己借给」谈话，说明英语能把一个给予动作变成关于「合不合适」的判断。

examples.en: He lent her his umbrella and walked home wet.
examples.cn: 他把伞借给她，自己淋着雨回家。

examples.en: The bank lends money to small firms at a fixed rate.
examples.cn: 银行按固定利率向小公司放贷。

examples.en: The quiet garden lends itself to long conversations.
examples.cn: 安静的花园很适合长谈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「懒得」——懒得还，就别开口借；lend 是借出，lent 是借出了。

root: 日耳曼语重构词根 laihwan（借出）→ 古英语 lǣnan（准许使用）与名词 lǣn → 中古英语 lenen → 现代英语 lend，过去式沿用古形 lent；与 loan 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is giving something for a time; the senses then split into money on credit, help and attention handed over, and the reflexive use for what suits a purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「暂时给予」；义项由此分出有息借贷的钱、交付出去的帮助与关注，以及表示「适合某用途」的反身用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand passing an umbrella across, still holding the handle until it comes back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把伞递过去，却一直虚握着伞柄，直到它回来。

branches.en: an umbrella changing hands at a doorway
branches.cn: 门口递过去的一把伞

branches.en: a bank counter counting notes for a small firm
branches.cn: 银行为小公司点钞的柜台

branches.en: a bench under a tree where talk runs long
branches.cn: 树下让人长谈的长椅

branches.en: a listener nodding without interrupting
branches.cn: 不打断、只点头的倾听者

branches.en: a returned umbrella and a thank-you note
branches.cn: 还回来的伞与一张道谢的便条

intro.en: The word is built from a Germanic root of lending, an Old English verb and its noun, and English endings that name the giver and the business.
intro.cn: 这个词由日耳曼语「借出」词根、古英语动词及其名词构成，再由英语词尾造出「出借者」和「这项业务」。

latinIntro.en: Lend belongs to the Germanic side of English and has no reliable Latin cognate, so no Latin entry is recorded here.
latinIntro.cn: lend 属于英语的日耳曼语部分，没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此这里不列拉丁条目。

definition_zh: 长度；长度单位；时长；程度；一段
definition_en: the measurement of something from end to end, its duration in time, the extent to which something is carried out, and a piece cut from something long
core_image: 卷尺从墙角拉到另一头，刻度停在木板的边缘
scene: 木匠把卷尺拉到墙角，低头看刻度，然后在木板上画下一道线。He measured the length of the table before cutting the board.
sceneCN: 这里是「长度」（第 1 个义项：从一端到另一端的量）；句意是他在裁板之前先量了桌子的长度。图中可辨识物件：卷尺、木板、铅笔与墙角。

pos.zh: 长度；时长；程度；一段

derivatives.zh: 由 length 加 -y 构成，义为「冗长的；漫长的」
由 length 加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「加长；变长」
由 length 与 wise 复合而成，义为「纵向地；沿长度方向」

senses.title: The measurement from end to end
senses.definition: the distance measured along something from one end to the other
senses.definitionCN: 沿某物从一端量到另一端的距离
senses.example: He measured the length of the table before cutting the board.
senses.exampleCN: 他在裁板之前量了桌子的长度。
senses.why: Old English lengþu was built from lang plus a suffix of abstract nouns, so the word names the quality a thing has by being long.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lengþu 由 lang（长）加抽象名词后缀构成，所以这个词指的就是事物「长」这一性质。

senses.title: The amount of time something lasts
senses.definition: the period during which something continues from start to finish
senses.definitionCN: 某件事从开始到结束所持续的时间
senses.example: The length of the film surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的时长让所有人都感到意外。
senses.why: Time is pictured as a line with two ends, so the same word for spatial extent is borrowed to measure how long an event runs.
senses.whyCN: 时间被想象成一条有两端的线，于是表示空间延展的同一个词被借来量一件事持续多久。

senses.title: The extent to which something is done
senses.definition: how fully or how far an action, argument or piece of writing is carried out
senses.definitionCN: 行动、论述或文章做到多完整、多深入
senses.example: The report discussed the causes at length.
senses.exampleCN: 报告详细讨论了各种原因。
senses.why: Just as a physical thing has a measurable extent, an argument can be carried to a certain extent, which gives the phrase at length its sense of full treatment.
senses.whyCN: 正如实物有可量的延展，一段论述也能被推进到某个「长度」，于是 at length 就有了「充分论述」的意思。

senses.title: A piece cut from something long
senses.definition: a measured piece of rope, pipe or cloth taken from a longer whole
senses.definitionCN: 从更长的整根绳、管或布上截下来的一段
senses.example: She cut a length of rope to tie the box.
senses.exampleCN: 她截了一段绳子来捆箱子。
senses.why: Once length names a measurable extent, a piece that has exactly that extent can itself be called a length, especially in rope and timber.
senses.whyCN: 既然 length 表示可量的长度，那么恰好具有这个长度的一段东西也就能被称为 a length，绳索与木料尤其如此。

intro.en: Length is the oldest English way of naming the quality of being long, formed from the adjective long with a suffix that builds abstract nouns.
intro.cn: length 是英语里指「长」这一性质最古老的说法，由形容词 long 加上构成抽象名词的后缀而来。

items.en: A reconstructed form dlonghos underlies the family of long words, and the same root appears in Latin longus, which is why the two branches look alike.
items.cn: 重构形式 dlonghos 是这一族「长」词的共同来源，同一词根也出现在拉丁语 longus，因此两条分支看起来相似。

items.en: Old English lang meant long in space and in time, and it could also describe a tall person.
items.cn: 古英语 lang 既指空间上的长，也指时间上的长，还能形容人个子高。

items.en: Adding the abstract suffix -þu to lang produced lengþu, the state or measure of being long.
items.cn: 在 lang 后加抽象名词后缀 -þu 得到 lengþu，即「长」的状态或量。

items.en: Middle English respelled the word with th and dropped the old ending, arriving at forms like lengthe.
items.cn: 中古英语把拼写改成 th 并丢掉旧词尾，出现了 lengthe 这样的形式。

items.en: Modern English settled on length, kept lengths as its plural, and extended the sense to duration and to a measured piece.
items.cn: 现代英语定为 length，复数 lengths，并把词义扩展到时长与截下的一段。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the adjectives and verbs built on the same long root; the near-meaning group collects words for measured extent and time span.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「长」词根上的形容词与动词；近义组收表示量度延展与时间跨度的词。

entries.definition: Lasting too long or taking more time than needed.
entries.definitionCN: 持续过久或比需要的更费时的。

entries.definition: To make something longer or to become longer.
entries.definitionCN: 使变长；变长。

entries.definition: The adjective from which length was built.
entries.definitionCN: 构成 length 的那个形容词。

entries.definition: Distance east or west on the earth, from the Latin word for length.
entries.definitionCN: 地球上的东西距离，来自拉丁语中表示「长度」的词。

entries.definition: The space between two points.
entries.definitionCN: 两点之间的空间。

entries.definition: The time during which something continues.
entries.definitionCN: 某事持续的时间。

entries.definition: The degree to which something reaches or is true.
entries.definitionCN: 某物达到的范围或真实程度。

entries.definition: The full distance or period from one end to the other.
entries.definitionCN: 从一端到另一端的全部距离或时段。

normalIntro.en: The word is the abstract noun of long, and its family keeps returning to measurement in space, measurement in time and the extent of an action.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 long 的抽象名词，同族词反复回到空间上的量、时间上的量，以及行动的推进程度。

normal.en: Length is long turned into a noun: if a thing is long, its length is the measure of that.
normal.cn: length 是把 long 变成名词：一个东西「长」，它的 length 就是这份长的量。

normal.en: The plural is lengths with th kept, not lengthths, so the spelling adds only an s after the th.
normal.cn: 复数是 lengths，th 保留不动，只在 th 后加 s。

normal.en: Lengthen adds -en to length and turns the measure back into an action of making longer.
normal.cn: lengthen 在 length 后加 -en，把「量」又变回「使之变长」的动作。

normal.en: Lengthy adds -y but carries a hint of criticism: more length than the situation needs.
normal.cn: lengthy 加 -y，却带一点批评意味：长度超过了场合所需。

normal.en: At length means two things at once: after a long time, and in full detail.
normal.cn: at length 同时有两个意思：经过很长时间之后，以及详细地。

abstract.en: The same word measures a table, a film and an argument, which shows how readily English maps time and reasoning onto space.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能量桌子、量影片、量论述，说明英语很自然地把时间和论证都投射到空间上。

abstract.en: A measured piece of rope is called a length, so the abstract measure becomes a concrete object when a knife cuts it.
abstract.cn: 截下的一段绳子也叫 a length，于是抽象的量在刀落下时变成了具体的物。

abstract.en: Long is the adjective of desire and length is its measure, but lengthy is the word we use when the desire has gone on too long.
abstract.cn: long 是表示渴望的形容词，length 是它的度量，而 lengthy 用在「拖得太久」的时候。

examples.en: He measured the length of the table before cutting the board.
examples.cn: 他在裁板之前量了桌子的长度。

examples.en: The length of the film surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 这部电影的时长让所有人都感到意外。

examples.en: She cut a length of rope to tie the box.
examples.cn: 她截了一段绳子来捆箱子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「愣是」——这根绳子愣是有三米长；记住 length 是长度。

root: 原始印欧语重构形式 dlonghos（长）→ 古英语 lang → 加抽象后缀 -þu 成 lengþu → 中古英语 lengthe → 现代英语 length；与拉丁语 longus 同出一源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the measure of being long; the senses then apply that measure to time, to how far an action is carried, and to a piece cut to that size.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「长」的量；义项再把这个量用到时间上、用到行动推进的程度上，以及用到恰好截成那么长的一段东西上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tape measure stretched from a corner to the far edge of a board.
core.cn: 核心意象：卷尺从墙角一直拉到木板的另一头。

branches.en: a tape measure lying along a plank
branches.cn: 沿木板铺开的卷尺

branches.en: a clock face marking a two-hour film
branches.cn: 标出一部两小时影片的钟面

branches.en: a report read slowly, page after page
branches.cn: 一页页慢慢读完的报告

branches.en: a coil of rope cut with a knife
branches.cn: 被刀截断的一盘绳

branches.en: a speaker who finally reaches the point
branches.cn: 终于讲到要点的说话人

intro.en: The word joins the adjective long to an Old English suffix for abstract nouns, and the family then adds endings for quality, action and direction.
intro.cn: 这个词把形容词 long 与古英语的抽象名词后缀接在一起，同族词再加上表示性质、动作与方向的词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: measuring much from end to end
items.meaningCN: 从一端到另一端很长的

definition_zh: 透镜；镜片；晶状体；镜头；视角
definition_en: a curved piece of glass or plastic that bends light, the matching part of the eye, the glass element of a camera, and a way of looking at a subject
core_image: 一枚弧形玻璃片把远处的灯光收成一个小亮点
scene: 摄影师的桌上，一枚弧形玻璃片被布擦得发亮，远处的灯在它里面缩成一点。He cleaned the lens before shooting the portrait.
sceneCN: 这里是「镜头」（第 3 个义项：相机上那片可更换的玻璃）；句意是他在拍人像之前先擦净了镜头。图中可辨识物件：擦镜布、弧形玻璃片、桌上的相机。

pos.zh: 透镜；镜片；晶状体；镜头；视角

derivatives.zh: 由 lens 与 man 复合而成，义为「摄影师；镜头工作者」
由 lens 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「无镜片的」
源自拉丁语小词 lenticula，义为「透镜状的；小扁豆形的」

senses.title: A curved piece of glass that bends light
senses.definition: a shaped piece of glass or plastic used to focus or spread light in an instrument
senses.definitionCN: 仪器中用来聚光或散光的成形玻璃片或塑料片
senses.example: The microscope needs a stronger lens to show the cells clearly.
senses.exampleCN: 显微镜需要更强的镜片才能把细胞看清。
senses.why: The word starts as the name of a lentil, because a biconvex piece of glass has the same plump oval shape as the seed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初只是「小扁豆」的名字，因为双凸的玻璃片和那颗种子一样呈饱满的椭圆。

senses.title: The light-focusing part of the eye
senses.definition: the small clear structure inside the eye that focuses images on the retina
senses.definitionCN: 眼球内把影像聚焦到视网膜上的透明小结构
senses.example: The lens of the eye focuses light onto the retina.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛的晶状体把光聚焦到视网膜上。
senses.why: Once lens names any shaped body that focuses light, the eye's own focusing body takes the same name by analogy of function.
senses.whyCN: 既然 lens 能指任何聚光的成形体，眼睛自带的聚光结构就按功能类比得到了同一个名字。

senses.title: The glass element of a camera
senses.definition: the glass unit fitted to a camera, often one of several that can be exchanged
senses.definitionCN: 装在相机上的玻璃组件，常为可更换的若干支之一
senses.example: He cleaned the lens before shooting the portrait.
senses.exampleCN: 他在拍人像之前先擦净了镜头。
senses.why: A camera is built around the same bending of light that a single lens performs, and the whole glass assembly simply borrows the part's name.
senses.whyCN: 相机正是围绕单片镜片所做的同一件弯光之事造出来的，于是整组玻璃组件干脆沿用了零件的名字。

senses.title: A way of looking at a subject
senses.definition: a particular standpoint that shapes how a subject is understood
senses.definitionCN: 决定人们如何理解某个主题的特定立场
senses.example: Viewed through the lens of history, the quarrel looks small.
senses.exampleCN: 从历史的视角看，那场争吵显得微不足道。
senses.why: A lens decides what enters the eye and how it is bent, so the word naturally becomes a metaphor for whatever selects and shapes our view.
senses.whyCN: 镜片决定什么进入眼睛、又如何被弯曲，于是这个词很自然地成了比喻，指那些筛选并塑造视野的东西。

intro.en: Lens is Latin for lentil; the optical sense was borrowed by seventeenth-century writers because a biconvex glass looked like the seed.
intro.cn: lens 在拉丁语里就是「小扁豆」；十七世纪的学者借它来指光学镜片，因为双凸玻璃的形状像那颗种子。

items.en: Lens, with the stem lent-, named the lentil, the small flat seed of a plant in the pea family.
items.cn: lens（词干 lent-）指小扁豆，即豆科植物那种小而扁的种子。

items.en: The diminutive lenticula named a small lentil and later supplied English lentil and the adjective lenticular.
items.cn: 小词形式 lenticula 指一颗小扁豆，后来为英语提供了 lentil 与形容词 lenticular。

items.en: Seventeenth-century writers of optics borrowed lens for a curved piece of glass, since a biconvex shape resembles a lentil.
items.cn: 十七世纪的光学作者借 lens 指弧形玻璃片，因为双凸形状与扁豆相似。

items.en: English took lens as a technical term of microscopy and astronomy, where curved glass was newly powerful.
items.cn: 英语把 lens 当作显微镜与天文学的技术术语引入，那时弧形玻璃刚刚显示出威力。

items.en: Modern English extended lens to the eye's own focusing body, to camera optics and to any selective point of view.
items.cn: 现代英语把 lens 扩展到眼睛自带的聚焦结构、相机光学，以及任何有筛选作用的视角。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the seed word behind the name and the forms built on it; the near-meaning group collects other optical parts that bend or split light.
note.cn: 形近组收这个名字背后的「种子」词及其派生形式；近义组收其他弯曲或分解光线的光学部件。

entries.definition: The small flat seed that gave the lens its name.
entries.definitionCN: 给透镜命名的这种小而扁的种子。

entries.definition: Shaped like a lentil or a lens.
entries.definitionCN: 形状像扁豆或透镜的。

entries.definition: A photographer or cameraman, especially in news work.
entries.definitionCN: 摄影师或摄影记者。

entries.definition: Made or working without a lens.
entries.definitionCN: 无镜片的；不用镜片工作的。

entries.definition: The hard transparent material that lenses are usually made from.
entries.definitionCN: 制作镜片常用的坚硬透明材料。

entries.definition: A shaped piece of glass that splits light into colours.
entries.definitionCN: 把光分解成多种颜色的成形玻璃。

entries.definition: A lens or device that makes small things look bigger.
entries.definitionCN: 使小东西看起来更大的镜片或装置。

entries.definition: The lens or lens group you look through in an instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器上供眼睛观看的那片或那组镜片。

normalIntro.en: The word is Latin for a seed, and the whole optical family keeps returning to that plump oval shape and to the bending of light.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词在拉丁语里是一颗种子，整个光学词族反复回到那个饱满的椭圆形状与弯折的光线。

normal.en: Latin lens means lentil, so the glass was named for its shape rather than for its function.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 lens 意为扁豆，所以这片玻璃是因形状得名，而不是因功能得名。

normal.en: Lentil and lens share one root: the seed and the glass are the same oval seen at different sizes.
normal.cn: lentil 与 lens 同根：种子与玻璃是同一个椭圆在不同尺度上的样子。

normal.en: Lenticular adds -ar to the Latin diminutive and means shaped like a lentil or a lens.
normal.cn: lenticular 在拉丁小词后加 -ar，意为「扁豆状或透镜状的」。

normal.en: Lensless adds -less: an instrument without that curved piece cannot focus anything.
normal.cn: lensless 加 -less：少了那片弧形玻璃，仪器就什么也聚不了。

normal.en: Through the lens of is the phrase to keep: it turns an optical part into a way of judging.
normal.cn: 要记住 through the lens of 这个说法：它把一片光学零件变成了一种评判方式。

abstract.en: A seed, a glass, an eye and a standpoint all answer to one word, because each of them selects and focuses what comes through.
abstract.cn: 种子、玻璃、眼睛与立场都由同一个词承担，因为它们都在筛选并聚焦穿过自己之物。

abstract.en: The history of lens shows how a name for shape can quietly become a name for power: the power to decide what is seen.
abstract.cn: lens 的历史说明，一个形状之名可以悄悄变成能力之名：决定什么能被看见的能力。

abstract.en: Calling a view a lens reminds us that no standpoint is perfectly clear glass; every one bends what it shows.
abstract.cn: 把视角称作 lens，提醒人没有任何立场是毫无偏折的玻璃，每一种都会弯折它所呈现的东西。

examples.en: The microscope needs a stronger lens to show the cells clearly.
examples.cn: 显微镜需要更强的镜片才能把细胞看清。

examples.en: The lens of the eye focuses light onto the retina.
examples.cn: 眼睛的晶状体把光聚焦到视网膜上。

examples.en: Viewed through the lens of history, the quarrel looks small.
examples.cn: 从历史的视角看，那场争吵显得微不足道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「棱子」——镜片边缘像棱子；记住 lens 是透镜、镜片。

root: 拉丁语 lens（小扁豆，词干 lent-）→ 十七世纪借作光学名词，因双凸镜片形似扁豆 → 现代英语扩展至晶状体、相机镜头与看待事物的视角。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a lentil-shaped glass that bends light; the senses then move to the eye's own focusing body, the camera's glass unit, and the metaphor of a selective standpoint.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是形似扁豆、弯折光线的玻璃；义项由此转到眼睛自带的聚焦结构、相机的玻璃组件，以及「有筛选作用的立场」这一比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small curved glass disc on a cloth, gathering a distant lamp into one bright point.
core.cn: 核心意象：布上一枚小小的弧形玻璃片，把远处的灯收成一个亮点。

branches.en: a glass disc bending a beam onto a slide
branches.cn: 把光束弯到载玻片上的玻璃片

branches.en: a pupil widening in a dim room
branches.cn: 暗房里慢慢张开的瞳孔

branches.en: a photographer wiping the front glass
branches.cn: 摄影师擦拭最前那片玻璃

branches.en: a historian reframing an old quarrel
branches.cn: 重新框定旧日争吵的历史学家

branches.en: a documentary filmed from one angle
branches.cn: 只从一个角度拍摄的纪录片

intro.en: The word is a Latin seed name, its diminutive and a Latin suffix, and English then builds the optical compounds and negatives that surround it.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「种子」名、它的小词形式与一个拉丁后缀构成，英语再围绕它造出光学复合词与否定义。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
