definition_zh: 有法律责任的；负有义务的；易于遭受的；很可能发生的
definition_en: legally responsible for something, or likely to do or suffer something
core_image: 一根绳子把签了名的契约系在一只脚踝上，另一头连着一块写着「赔偿」的木牌
scene: 保险公司在条款中写明，运输途中货物受损时由承运人承担赔偿。The policy states that the carrier is liable for damage to the goods while they are in transit.
sceneCN: 这里指「依法对某项损害承担赔偿」，对应第 1 个义项：因契约或法律而被绑定、必须负责；句意为条款规定运输途中货物受损由承运人负责。画面要点：签名的契约、系在脚踝上的绳、写着「赔偿」的木牌。

pos.zh: 有法律责任的；负有义务的；易于…的；很可能…的（多作表语，后接表示对象或方向的介词）

derivatives.zh: 责任；债务（形容词加表性质的名词后缀，由「可被约束的」转为「须承担的法律责任」）
各项债务（名词加复数词尾，指账面上须偿付的多项义务）
有限责任（形容词与名词构成的复合术语，指以出资额为限的责任形式）

senses.title: Legally answerable for damage
senses.titleCN: 对损害依法负有赔偿责任
senses.definition: bound by law or contract to pay for loss or injury one has caused
senses.definitionCN: 依法或依契约必须为自己造成的损失或伤害作出赔偿
senses.example: The policy states that the carrier is liable for damage to the goods while they are in transit.
senses.exampleCN: 条款规定，运输途中货物受损由承运人负责赔偿。
senses.why: The word began as 'able to be bound', and a contract is exactly the rope that binds a party to answer for a loss.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初意为「可被绑住的」，而契约正是那根把一方绑住、使其对损失负责的绳子。

senses.title: Answerable for a debt
senses.definition: obliged to settle a debt or to perform an undertaking, often because one has guaranteed it
senses.definitionCN: 必须清偿债务或履行承诺，常因本人曾为之作保
senses.example: A guarantor is liable for the loan if the borrower defaults.
senses.exampleCN: 借款人违约时，担保人对该笔贷款负有责任。
senses.why: Money makes the bond visible: the rope now runs to a specific sum that must be paid.
senses.whyCN: 金钱让这根绳子看得见：它现在连着一个必须偿付的具体数额。

senses.title: Subject to a penalty or a charge
senses.definition: exposed by law to a fine, a tax or some other imposed charge
senses.definitionCN: 依法可能被课以罚款、税款或其他征收
senses.example: Income above that threshold is liable to tax.
senses.exampleCN: 超过该门槛的收入应纳税。
senses.why: The bond can run toward an authority rather than a victim, so the same word covers what the state may exact.
senses.whyCN: 这根绳子也可以通向权力机关而不是受害者，因此同一个词也覆盖国家可以征收的部分。

senses.title: Exposed to harm
senses.definition: open to a particular risk, such as injury, loss or damage, because of circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 因所处情况而暴露于某种风险，如受伤、损失或损坏
senses.example: Low-lying fields are liable to flooding in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 低洼的田地在春天容易遭水淹。
senses.why: From 'bound to answer' the word loosens into 'open to', a shift from a legal tie to a physical exposure.
senses.whyCN: 从「必须负责」松弛为「暴露于」，这是从法律束缚向身体处境的转移。

senses.title: Likely to happen
senses.definition: probable, especially of something unwelcome that may occur
senses.definitionCN: 很可能发生，尤指可能发生的不快之事
senses.example: The bridge is liable to close when the wind rises.
senses.exampleCN: 风一大，这座桥就可能关闭。
senses.why: If a thing is exposed to a risk, it will often meet it, so exposure slides into probability.
senses.whyCN: 如果一物暴露于某种风险，它往往会遇上，于是「暴露」滑向「概率」。

senses.title: Prone to do something
senses.definition: having a tendency to act in a certain way, often unintentionally or regrettably
senses.definitionCN: 有以某种方式行事的倾向，常指无意或令人遗憾的行为
senses.example: He is liable to forget names under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 他在压力之下容易忘记名字。
senses.why: A person can be bound to an outcome by his own habits, so the word moves from outer obligation to inner tendency.
senses.whyCN: 人可能被自己的习惯绑向某个结果，因此这个词从外在义务移向内在倾向。

senses.title: Obliged to serve
senses.titleCN: 有义务服役或尽某项义务
senses.definition: required by law to perform a service, such as military duty or statutory work
senses.definitionCN: 依法须履行某项服务，如兵役或法定工作
senses.example: All men of that age were liable for military service.
senses.exampleCN: 那个年龄的所有男子都有服兵役的义务。
senses.why: The bond here is to the state and to a duty rather than to a creditor, but the grammar of being bound is unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 这里的绳子通向国家与一项义务，而不是通向债权人，但「被绑住」的语法没有变。

senses.title: Mildly probable in speech
senses.definition: used informally to mean that something may well happen, with less force than a prediction
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示某事很可能发生，语气比预测更弱
senses.example: She is liable to be late if the traffic is bad.
senses.exampleCN: 如果交通不好，她可能会迟到。
senses.why: In everyday speech the legal weight drains away, leaving only a softened forecast that keeps a trace of the old 'bound to happen'.
senses.whyCN: 在日常口语中，法律分量被抽走，只剩一个软化的预测，仍留着「注定会发生」的一丝痕迹。

intro.en: Liable comes from Old French lier 'to bind', from Latin ligare, with the adjective ending -able. It first meant 'able to be bound', then 'bound by law to answer', and later widened to exposure and probability.
intro.cn: liable 出自古法语 lier「捆绑」，源头为拉丁语 ligare，加上形容词后缀 -able。它最初意为「可被绑住的」，继而指「依法须负责的」，后扩展到「暴露于」与「很可能」。

items.en: Ligare 'to bind' is the verb behind the word; the same root also produced alliance, obligation and ligament.
items.cn: ligare 意为「捆绑」，是这个词背后的动词；同一词根还产生了「联盟」「义务」与「韧带」。

items.en: Old French lier carried the verb into English, and its participle gave the sense of something or someone bound.
items.cn: 古法语 lier 把这个动词带入英语，其分词给出「被绑住的」这一意思。

items.en: The adjective formed with the ending for 'able' meant 'able to be bound', at first in the sense of being bound by law to answer for something.
items.cn: 加上表示「可…的」后缀构成的形容词，意为「可被绑住的」，最初指依法须对某事负责。

items.en: In medieval and early modern law the word described a person bound to pay or to answer, and fixed phrases named the object of the bond.
items.cn: 在中世纪与近代早期的法律中，这个词描述被绑定须付款或须作答的人，固定搭配则指明被绑向的对象。

items.en: The widening from 'bound to answer' to 'exposed to' and then to 'likely to' happened gradually, and the first date of the looser use is uncertain.
items.cn: 从「必须负责」扩展到「暴露于」再到「很可能」，这一过程是渐进的，较松弛用法首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group contains words that look or sound close but come from other sources or carry other senses; the second group gives near alternatives for responsibility and for proneness.
note.cn: 第一组是形音相近但来源不同或另有含义的词；第二组是「责任」与「易于」两个方向的近义替代。

entries.definition: A published false statement that damages a reputation; it comes from a Latin word for a small book, not from the verb to bind.
entries.definitionCN: 公开发表、损害名誉的不实陈述；它出自拉丁语中表示小册子的词，与「捆绑」无关。

entries.definition: Able to be trusted; it is formed from the verb rely plus the same ending, and has nothing to do with legal responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 可信赖的；它由动词「依赖」加同一个后缀构成，与法律责任无关。

entries.definition: Unstable or easily changed, used in chemistry and psychology; its Latin source means 'sliding', not 'binding'.
entries.definitionCN: 不稳定、易变的，用于化学与心理学；它的拉丁来源意为「滑动」，而不是「捆绑」。

entries.definition: Having a duty to deal with something and being answerable for it; it is wider than the entry word and need not be legal.
entries.definitionCN: 有义务处理某事并须为之负责；它比本词宽，而且不必是法律上的。

entries.definition: Required to explain or justify one's actions to a person or body; it stresses reporting upward rather than paying for loss.
entries.definitionCN: 须向某人或机构解释、交代自己的行为；它强调向上报告，而不是赔偿损失。

entries.definition: Likely to suffer from or to do something, usually something bad; it covers the exposure sense but carries no legal duty.
entries.definitionCN: 易遭受或易做出某事，通常是不好的事；它覆盖「暴露」这一义，却不带法律义务。

entries.definition: Likely to do something, often in a neutral or habitual way; it lacks the sense of risk that the entry word usually carries.
entries.definitionCN: 有做某事的倾向，常为中性的或习惯性的；它缺少本词通常带的「风险」意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verb to bind, the adjective ending for 'able', real derived words and real legal phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「捆绑」的动词、表示「可…的」形容词后缀、真实派生词与真实法律用语。

normal.en: The core is a rope: liable means able to be bound, and a contract is the rope.
normal.cn: 核心是一根绳子：本词意为「可被绑住的」，而契约就是那根绳。

normal.en: The family runs liability, liabilities and limited liability.
normal.cn: 同族词包括责任、各项债务与有限责任。

normal.en: The preposition sorts the senses: liable for a loss, liable to a penalty or a flood.
normal.cn: 介词把义项分开：对损失负责，应受处罚或易遭水淹。

normal.en: The same root appears in alliance, obligation and ligament, all forms of binding.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在联盟、义务与韧带中，都是不同形式的「绑」。

normal.en: In speech the legal rope goes slack, and liable becomes a soft way of saying likely.
normal.cn: 在口语中法律之绳松脱，这个词变成「很可能」的软说法。

abstract.en: Picture a signed paper tied to an ankle, so that wherever the person walks the obligation follows.
abstract.cn: 想象一张签了名的纸系在脚踝上，人走到哪里，义务就跟到哪里。

abstract.en: Picture a field lying low beside a river, exposed each spring without anyone having agreed to it.
abstract.cn: 想象河边的低洼田地，每年春天都被淹，而没有任何人同意过这件事。

abstract.en: Picture a rope that slowly turns into a probability, still tied but no longer pulled by a court.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子慢慢变成一种概率，仍然系着，却不再被法庭拉动。

examples.en: The manufacturer is liable for defects found within two years.
examples.cn: 制造商对两年内发现的缺陷负有责任。

examples.en: Drivers are liable to heavy fines for using a phone at the wheel.
examples.cn: 司机开车时使用电话可能被重罚。

examples.en: The old roof is liable to leak after a long storm.
examples.cn: 旧屋顶在长时间暴雨之后容易漏水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赖不了的」——签了字就得赔，绳子系在脚上，赖也赖不掉，所以是有责任的。

root: 古法语 lier「捆绑」← 拉丁语 ligare「捆绑」→ 加表示「可…的」后缀构成 liable，字面为「可被绑住的」。ligare 的更深来源一般认为是印欧语中表示「系、缠」的词根，相关形式属重构形式；同根词包括 alliance、obligation、ligament。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings unwind from one rope. Bound by a contract gives legal responsibility and debts; bound toward an authority gives penalties, taxes and service; loosening the rope gives exposure to harm, then likelihood and personal tendency; and in casual speech the rope nearly disappears, leaving only a soft forecast.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一根绳子解开。被契约绑住，产生法律责任与债务；被绑向权力机关，产生处罚、税款与服役义务；绳子一松，产生暴露于损害、可能性与个人倾向；到了口语里绳子几乎消失，只剩一个软化的预测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed obligation tied to the ankle, following the person wherever he goes.
core.cn: 核心意象：系在脚踝上的签名义务，人走到哪里它就跟到哪里。

branches.en: BOUND: legal answerability for damage, and the duty to settle a debt.
branches.cn: 被绑住：对损害的依法负责，以及清偿债务的义务。

branches.en: OWED TO AUTHORITY: penalties and taxes on one side, service to the state on the other.
branches.cn: 欠向权力：一边是处罚与税款，一边是对国家的服役义务。

branches.en: EXPOSED: open to injury, loss or damage because of where one stands.
branches.cn: 暴露：因所处位置而易于受伤、受损或遭损失。

branches.en: LIKELY AND PRONE: what probably happens, and what a person tends to do.
branches.cn: 可能与倾向：很可能发生的事，以及一个人容易做出的举动。

branches.en: LOOSE FORECAST: the everyday weakening of the word into a mild 'may well'.
branches.cn: 松脱的预测：日常用法中弱化为轻微的「很可能」。

intro.en: One Latin verb for binding underlies the word and a large neighbouring family; the adjective ending adds the idea of capacity, and later endings build nouns and verbs for obligations.
intro.cn: 一个表示「捆绑」的拉丁动词支撑着这个词与一大片相邻词族；形容词后缀加上「能力」之意，后来的后缀又构成表示义务的名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below show the verb of binding and its compounds; the English words built on them keep the same physical image of a tie.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式展示表示「捆绑」的动词及其复合形式；由它们构成的英语词都保留同一种「系绑」的实体意象。

items.meaning: able to be bound, hence answerable
items.meaningCN: 可被绑住的，因而须负责的
items.example: The carrier is liable for the loss.
items.exampleCN: 承运人对该损失负有责任。

items.example: The firm accepted liability for the accident.
items.exampleCN: 公司承认对该事故负有责任。

items.meaning: debts shown on a balance sheet
items.meaningCN: 资产负债表上列出的各项债务
items.example: The company's liabilities exceeded its assets.
items.exampleCN: 公司的债务超过了资产。

items.example: The two states allied against the fleet.
items.exampleCN: 两国结盟对抗那支舰队。

items.meaningCN: 依协议形成的正式联合
items.example: The alliance held through the winter.
items.exampleCN: 这个联盟维持了整个冬天。

items.meaning: to bind someone by duty or favour
items.meaningCN: 以义务或恩惠约束某人
items.example: The contract obliges the seller to deliver.
items.exampleCN: 合同使卖方负有交付义务。

items.meaning: a duty one is bound to perform
items.example: The lease sets out the tenant's obligations.
items.exampleCN: 租约列明了租户的义务。

items.meaning: a band that binds bones together
items.meaningCN: 把骨骼系连起来的韧带
items.example: The runner tore a ligament in his knee.
items.exampleCN: 跑者撕裂了膝部的一条韧带。

items.meaning: a tie or band, also joined letters
items.example: The surgeon applied a ligature to the vessel.
items.exampleCN: 外科医生用系带结扎了那条血管。

latinEntries.meaning: to bind, to put under obligation

derivatives.zh: 责任；债务（形容词加表性质的名词后缀，由「可被约束的」转为「须承担的法律责任」）
各项债务（名词加复数词尾，指账面上须偿付的多项义务）
义务（由同根的「使受约束」动词加表行为的名词后缀构成，指必须履行的事）
联盟（由同根的「系到一处」动词加表行为的名词后缀构成，指依协议形成的联合）

definition_zh: 自由主义的；开明的；慷慨的；宽松的；人文学科的
definition_en: open to different views, favouring political reform, generous in amount, not strict or literal, or relating to a broad education in the arts and sciences
core_image: 一个不被绳索束缚的人，伸手把东西分给别人
scene: 社区听证会上，一位议员支持为低收入家庭增建住房。The liberal member spoke for more low-income housing and argued that the planning rules should be looser.
sceneCN: 这里 liberal 是「政治立场偏自由派、支持改革的」（第 2 个义项：政治上的自由主义）；句意：这位自由派议员支持为低收入家庭增建住房，并主张规划规则应当更宽松。图中可辨识物件：听证会标牌、麦克风、住房规划图、选民登记表。

pos.zh: 自由主义的；开明的；慷慨的；宽松的；人文教育的
自由主义者；自由派支持者

derivatives.zh: 慷慨地；大量地；开明地
自由主义
使自由化；放宽限制
不宽容的；反自由的

senses.title: Open to different views
senses.titleCN: 开明的：能容纳不同意见
senses.definition: willing to accept and tolerate behaviour or opinions different from one's own
senses.definitionCN: 愿意接受并容忍与自己不同的行为或观点
senses.example: Her parents were liberal about curfews, as long as she called home.
senses.exampleCN: 她父母对宵禁时间很开明，只要她打电话回家就行。
senses.why: The core is Latin liber 'free'. A liberal mind is not bound by a narrow rule or prejudice; it leaves room for what it did not expect.
senses.whyCN: 核心是拉丁语 liber“自由的”。开明的头脑不被狭窄的规矩或偏见捆住，会为意料之外的东西留出空间。

senses.title: Politically reform-minded
senses.definition: favouring social reform, individual rights and government action, often associated with the centre-left
senses.definitionCN: 支持社会改革、个人权利与政府作为，常与中左政治立场相关
senses.example: The liberal party lost its rural seats in the election.
senses.exampleCN: 自由派政党在选举中失去了乡村选区。
senses.why: In 19c politics liberal meant free from arbitrary rule and favouring constitutional government. The label later shifted toward social reform, and its meaning still varies by country.
senses.whyCN: 在 19 世纪政治中，liberal 指免于专断统治、支持宪政。这个标签后来偏向社会改革，其含义至今因国家而异。

senses.title: Generous in amount
senses.definition: given or existing in large amounts; more than enough
senses.definitionCN: 给予或存在的量大；足够而有余
senses.example: Add a liberal amount of olive oil before roasting.
senses.exampleCN: 烤之前加足量的橄榄油。
senses.why: Latin liberalis already meant 'generous, munificent'. The free man was expected to give freely, so the adjective moved from social status to quantity.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 liberalis 本就有“慷慨、大方”之义。自由人被认为应当大方给予，于是形容词从社会身份滑到了数量。

senses.title: Not strictly literal
senses.definition: not strictly literal or exact; allowing freedom in interpretation or wording
senses.definitionCN: 不严格依照字面或精确表述；在解释或措辞上留出自由
senses.example: The translator took a liberal reading of the poem's last line.
senses.exampleCN: 译者对诗的最后一行作了较自由的解读。
senses.why: Freedom applies to wording: a liberal translation or interpretation departs from the letter in order to keep the sense.
senses.whyCN: 自由落在措辞上：liberal translation 或 interpretation 离开字面，为的是保住意思。

senses.title: Of a broad education in the arts
senses.titleCN: 博雅教育的：人文学科的
senses.definition: relating to a broad education in humanities, social sciences and sciences rather than narrow technical training
senses.definitionCN: 与人文、社会科学和自然科学的广博教育有关，而非狭窄的技术训练
senses.example: He studied liberal arts before law school.
senses.exampleCN: 他在法学院之前读的是人文学科。
senses.why: artes liberales were the skills befitting a free citizen, as opposed to a slave or a tradesman. Liberal arts still names that ideal of a broad, non-vocational education.
senses.whyCN: artes liberales 是“配得上自由公民的技艺”，区别于奴隶或工匠的技能。liberal arts 至今指这种广博而非职业化的教育理想。

senses.title: Noun: a person of liberal views
senses.definition: a person who holds liberal political or social views
senses.definitionCN: 持自由派政治或社会观点的人
senses.example: The bill split the liberals in the senate.
senses.exampleCN: 这项议案让参议院里的自由派分裂了。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a countable noun by metonymy: a person is named by the position they hold. Politics is the usual setting for this use.
senses.whyCN: 形容词通过转喻变成可数名词：用一个人所持的立场来指这个人。这种用法通常出现在政治语境。

senses.title: Free-market economics
senses.titleCN: 经济上的自由市场主张
senses.definition: favouring free markets, private ownership and little state control, in the classical economic sense
senses.definitionCN: 在古典经济学意义上支持自由市场、私有制与较少的国家控制
senses.example: The party is liberal on trade but cautious on welfare.
senses.exampleCN: 该党在贸易上主张自由，在福利上却谨慎。
senses.why: Classical liberalism put economic freedom alongside political freedom. Note the trap: in US politics 'liberal' often means the opposite on economic policy, so the sense depends on context.
senses.whyCN: 古典自由主义把经济自由与政治自由并列。注意陷阱：在美国政治语境中，liberal 在经济政策上常指相反方向，因此词义要看上下文。

senses.title: Liberal with: giving freely
senses.definition: generous in giving something to other people, sometimes to the point of excess
senses.definitionCN: 在给予他人某物时很大方，有时到了过分的程度
senses.example: He was liberal with praise and stingy with details.
senses.exampleCN: 他夸人毫不吝啬，给细节却很小气。
senses.why: Here the quantity sense is directed at people. Liberal with praise means the giving hand opens wide; the same phrase can quietly criticize someone who gives too freely.
senses.whyCN: 这里数量义对准了人。liberal with praise 意味着给予的手张得很开；同一短语也可以暗含批评，指某人给得过头。

senses.title: Not strict: allowing latitude
senses.definition: not strictly enforced or tightly controlled; allowing freedom of action
senses.definitionCN: 不被严格执行或 tightly 控制；允许行动自由
senses.example: The school has a liberal policy on mobile phones.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校对手机的规定很宽松。
senses.why: The freedom is now built into an arrangement, not into a person's mind. A liberal policy leaves the margin wide, which is why the word can describe rules as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 这时自由被写进了安排本身，而不是某人的头脑。宽松的政策把余地留得很宽，因此这个词既能形容人，也能形容规则。

intro.en: Liberal comes from Latin liber 'free', not from liber 'book'. Its oldest English sense was 'generous, noble', and 'free' ran through both the social and the educational branches.
intro.cn: liberal 出自拉丁语 liber“自由的”，不是 liber“书”。它最早的英语义是“慷慨、高贵”，而“自由”贯穿了社会与教育这两条分支。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'generous, noble, free', especially of a person of high birth or a free citizen.
items.cn: 最早记录于 14 世纪中期的英语，意为“慷慨的、高贵的、自由的”，尤指出身高贵者或自由公民。

items.en: liberalis 'of a free person, noble, generous, munificent' is formed from liber 'free' plus -alis.
items.cn: liberalis“属于自由人的、高贵的、慷慨的”由 liber“自由的”加 -alis 构成。

items.en: liber 'free' and liber 'book' are two different nouns. Library comes from librarium 'bookcase', built on liber 'book / inner bark', so library is not a relative of liberal.
items.cn: liber“自由的”与 liber“书”是两个不同的名词。library 出自 librarium“书柜”，建在 liber“书／树内皮”上，因此 library 不是 liberal 的亲戚。

items.en: artes liberales were 'the arts befitting a free person', the broad curriculum of grammar, rhetoric, logic, arithmetic, geometry, music and astronomy. English liberal arts is a calque of that phrase.
items.cn: artes liberales 是“配得上自由人的技艺”，包括语法、修辞、逻辑、算术、几何、音乐与天文这一广博课程。英语 liberal arts 就是该短语的仿译。

items.en: liber is connected with PIE *leudh- 'free, grow' (some sources gloss it 'people'). This reconstruction is generally accepted rather than certain.
items.cn: liber 与原始印欧语 *leudh-“自由、成长”相联系（也有资料解作“人民”）。这一重构属于一般认为是，并非确证。

items.en: The political sense develops in the 19c around constitutional government and free trade. In 20c US English liberal came to mean social reform and state action, which is why the word can sound opposite in different countries. It is never related to licere 'be permitted' (license).
items.cn: 政治义在 19 世纪围绕宪政与自由贸易发展起来。到 20 世纪美国英语中，liberal 转指社会改革与国家作为，因此这个词在不同国家听起来可能相反。它与 licere“被允许”（license）从无关系。

note.en: The look-alike group turns on the two different Latins: liber 'free' gives liberty, liberate and liberal, while liber 'book' gives library. The near-meaning group separates the political label from attitude and amount words.
note.cn: 形近组的关键是两个不同的拉丁词：liber“自由的”给出 liberty、liberate、liberal，而 liber“书”给出 library。近义组把政治标签与态度词、数量词分开。

entries.definition: freedom from control or restriction. It is the abstract noun of liber 'free', the same source as liberal.
entries.definitionCN: 免于控制或限制的自由。它是 liber“自由的”的抽象名词，与 liberal 同源。

entries.definition: to set someone free from control, prison or occupation. It is the verb from liberare, the same 'free' family.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人摆脱控制、监禁或占领。它出自 liberare，属于同一个“自由”词族。

entries.definition: a place where books are kept. It looks like liberal, but it comes from liber 'book / inner bark' through librarium, not from liber 'free'.
entries.definitionCN: 藏书的地方。它形似 liberal，却出自 liber“书／树内皮”经 librarium 演变，不是 liber“自由的”。

entries.definition: favouring reform or new ideas, often more activist than liberal. It is a political label, not a word for generosity or education.
entries.definitionCN: 支持改革或新观念的，通常比 liberal 更行动派。它是政治标签，不表示慷慨或教育。

entries.definition: willing to accept differences. It names the attitude itself and carries no political programme.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意接受差异的。它只指态度本身，不携带政治纲领。

entries.definition: giving much or containing much. It overlaps liberal in amount and giving, but has no political or educational sense.
entries.definitionCN: 给予很多或含量充足的。它在数量与给予义上与 liberal 重叠，但没有政治或教育义。

entries.definition: willing to consider new ideas. It is more personal and less ideological than liberal.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意考虑新观念的。它比 liberal 更个人化，意识形态色彩更弱。

normalIntro.en: Real parts: liber 'free' + -alis, with liberty, liberate and deliver in the same family. The look-alike library belongs to liber 'book' and must be kept apart.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：liber“自由的”+ -alis，同族有 liberty、liberate、deliver。形近的 library 属于 liber“书”，必须分开。

normal.en: liber 'free' is the stem: liberal, liberty, liberate and deliver all carry some form of 'freeing'.
normal.cn: liber“自由的”是词干：liberal、liberty、liberate、deliver 都带有某种“使自由”的意思。

normal.en: artes liberales were the skills of a free citizen, which is why liberal arts means a broad education rather than a political opinion.
normal.cn: artes liberales 是自由公民的技艺，所以 liberal arts 指广博教育，而不是政治观点。

normal.en: library comes from liber 'book', a different noun. A library is a book-place, not a freedom-place.
normal.cn: library 出自另一个名词 liber“书”。图书馆是放书的地方，不是放自由的地方。

normal.en: deliver is de- 'away' + liberare 'free': to deliver a parcel is to free it from your hands into someone else's.
normal.cn: deliver 是 de-“离开”+ liberare“使自由”：把包裹交付出去，就是让它离开你的手、到别人手里。

normal.en: liberal with praise uses the generosity branch, not the political one: the hand gives freely.
normal.cn: liberal with praise 走的是“慷慨”分支，不是政治分支：手在大方地给。

abstract.en: Picture a gate with no lock: a person can walk out, and because they can walk out, they can also leave room for others to walk in. Liberal is that unlocked gate, applied to minds, rules and money.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没有锁的门：人能走出去，也正因为能走出去，才会给别人留出走进来的余地。liberal 就是这扇没锁的门，用在头脑、规则与金钱上。

abstract.en: Freedom can be spent in three directions: given away as generosity, kept open as tolerance, or written into a curriculum as the education of a free person.
abstract.cn: 自由可以花在三个方向：作为慷慨被给出去，作为宽容被留开，或作为自由人的教育被写进课程。

abstract.en: The same word can mean 'leave it loose' and 'give a lot'. Both are the image of a hand that does not close.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可以指“放宽”，也可以指“给得多”。两者都是同一幅图：一只不握紧的手。

examples.en: A liberal education taught her to question her own assumptions.
examples.cn: 博雅教育教会她质疑自己的预设。

examples.en: Pour a liberal amount of sauce over the fish.
examples.cn: 在鱼上浇足量的酱汁。

examples.en: He is socially liberal but fiscally conservative.
examples.cn: 他在社会议题上开明，在财政上保守。

dict_mnemonic.text: “离不了”——离不了自由，凡事主张放开 → liberal 自由的、开明的

root: 拉丁语 liber“自由的”（不是 liber“书”）+ -alis，核心是“不受束缚的、像自由人那样给予”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of liberal, all variations on 'not bound': a mind not bound by prejudice, a politics of reform, a hand that gives widely, a reading not bound to the letter, an education for a free person, and rules left loose.
sensesIntro.cn: liberal 的九个义项都是“不受束缚”的变体：不被偏见捆住的头脑、改革的政治、给得宽的手、不囿于字面的解读、自由人的教育，以及留得很松的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unbound person, whose hand is free to give and whose mind is free to admit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个未被捆住的人，手可以自由给予，头脑可以自由接纳。

branches.en: OPEN AND LOOSE: the same freedom applied to a mind and to a set of rules.
branches.cn: 开明与宽松：同一种自由，用在头脑上，也用在规则上。

branches.en: POLITICS AND ECONOMY: the reform label, the person who wears it, and the free-market branch.
branches.cn: 政治与经济：改革标签、持标签的人，以及自由市场分支。

branches.en: GENEROSITY: abundance in amount, and the open hand that gives to people.
branches.cn: 慷慨：数量上的充足，以及向人张开的手。

branches.en: INTERPRETATION: freedom from the literal letter in reading and translation.
branches.cn: 解释：在阅读与翻译中摆脱字面的束缚。

branches.en: EDUCATION: artes liberales, the broad curriculum of a free person.
branches.cn: 教育：artes liberales，自由人的广博课程。

intro.en: Liberal takes ordinary English suffixes: -ly for the adverb, -ism for the system, -ize for the verb, and il- as a negative prefix before l.
intro.cn: liberal 接的是普通英语后缀：-ly 构成副词，-ism 构成主义，-ize 构成动词，il- 则在 l 前作否定前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family of liber 'free' includes liberty, liberate, deliver and libertine. Library belongs to the other liber, 'book', and is not part of this family.
latinIntro.cn: liber“自由的”这一拉丁词族包括 liberty、liberate、deliver、libertine。library 属于另一个 liber“书”，不在这个词族里。

items.meaning: generously, in large amounts, or in an open-minded way
items.meaningCN: 慷慨地；大量地；开明地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Apply the cream liberally to the burned area.
items.exampleCN: 在烫伤处大量涂抹药膏。

items.meaning: the political and economic doctrine of liberal ideas
items.meaningCN: 自由主义（-ism 构成主义、学说）
items.exampleCN: 古典自由主义支持自由贸易。

items.meaning: to make rules or systems less strict
items.meaningCN: 使自由化；放宽（-ize 表示“使……”）
items.example: The government liberalized the visa rules.

items.meaning: not tolerant of different views; opposed to liberal ideas
items.meaningCN: 不宽容的；反自由的（il- 是否定前缀）
items.example: The ban was criticized as illiberal.
items.exampleCN: 这项禁令被批评为不宽容。

items.example: The adjective sits at the centre of liberal and liberty.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是 liberal 与 liberty 的共同核心。

items.example: It carries the free adjective into English as liberal.
items.exampleCN: 它把“自由”这个形容词带进英语成为 liberal。

items.structure: suffix naming a system or movement
items.meaning: a body of doctrine or practice
items.example: It forms liberalism, the political doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 liberalism 这一政治学说。

items.example: It forms liberality, the quality of being generous or open.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 liberality，即慷慨或开明的品质。

items.example: The army liberated the city at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 军队在黎明时解放了这座城市。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 自由；免于控制（-tas 构成抽象名词，经法语入英语）

latinEntries.meaning: to set someone or something free
latinEntries.meaningCN: 解放；使自由（出自 liberare“使自由”）

latinEntries.meaning: to hand over, save, or set free; literally 'to free away'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 交付；解救；字面“使脱离而自由”（de- + liberare）

latinEntries.meaning: a person without moral restraint; originally a freed slave
latinEntries.meaningCN: 放荡者；原指被释放的奴隶（自由义走偏为“无约束”）

definition_zh: 解放；使获得自由；释放；解除束缚
definition_en: to set a person or place free from control, or to release something that was held back
core_image: 牢门上的铁锁被剪断，门向外推开，光落到台阶上
scene: 城门在清晨被推开，围在广场上的人群让出一条路，被关押多年的人慢慢走出来。The soldiers liberated the town at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里是「解放」（第 1 个义项：使一个地方脱离控制）；句意为士兵们在黎明时解放了这座城镇。图中可辨识物件：推开的城门、让路的人群、石阶上的光。

pos.zh: 解放；使获得自由；释放；解除束缚

derivatives.zh: 由 liberate 去 e 加 -ion 构成，义为「解放；释放」
由 liberate 加 -or 构成，义为「解放者」
由现在分词转成的形容词，义为「令人感到解脱的」
由过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已获解放的；思想开放的」

senses.title: To free a place or its people from outside control
senses.definition: to drive an occupying power or an oppressive force out of a place and its people
senses.definitionCN: 把占领者或压迫性力量从一个地方及其人民身上赶走
senses.example: The soldiers liberated the town at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们在黎明时解放了这座城镇。
senses.why: Latin liber meant free, and the verb liberare made that state happen; the object here is a whole community, so the word names a collective act of freeing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 liber 意为自由的，动词 liberare 就是让这种状态发生；这里的对象是整个群体，所以这个词指的是一次集体的解救行动。

senses.title: To set a prisoner or captive free
senses.definition: to open the way out for a person held in prison or captivity
senses.definitionCN: 为被关押或囚禁的人打开出去的路
senses.example: The rebels liberated every prisoner in the jail.
senses.exampleCN: 起义者把监狱里的囚犯全部释放了。
senses.why: The same verb turns from a town to a single body behind bars; freedom is now measured by a door that opens for one person.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词从一座城转到铁栏后的一个身体；此时的自由，衡量的就是有一扇门为这一个人打开。

senses.title: To free someone from something that limits them
senses.definition: to free a person from a habit, fear or narrow way of thinking that holds them back
senses.definitionCN: 使人从阻碍自己的习惯、恐惧或狭隘想法中脱身
senses.example: Travel liberated her from a narrow view of the world.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行把她从狭隘的世界观里解放出来。
senses.why: Here the prison is invisible: what holds a person is a habit or an idea, and the verb works by loosening that grip rather than by breaking a lock.
senses.whyCN: 这里的牢笼看不见：困住一个人的是习惯或观念，动词的作用是松开这只手，而不是砸开一把锁。

senses.title: To release something stored or bound
senses.definition: to set loose a gas, heat or energy that was held in a substance or a system
senses.definitionCN: 把原本束缚在某种物质或系统中的气体、热量或能量放出来
senses.example: The reaction liberates heat and light.
senses.exampleCN: 这个反应释放出热和光。
senses.why: Chemistry keeps the oldest image in plain sight: what was bound inside a compound is let go, exactly as a prisoner is let out of a cell.
senses.whyCN: 化学把最古老的画面摆得明明白白：原本被束缚在化合物里的东西被放开，就像囚犯被放出牢房。

intro.en: Liberate is built from a Latin adjective for free plus a verb ending, and its family has carried the idea of freedom through law, politics and chemistry.
intro.cn: liberate 由拉丁语中表示「自由」的形容词加动词词尾构成，这一族词把「自由」的观念从法律带到政治，再带到化学。

items.en: Liber was an adjective meaning free, and as a noun it named a free person as opposed to a slave.
items.cn: liber 是表示「自由的」形容词，作名词时指自由人，与奴隶相对。

items.en: Liberare meant to set free or to release, and it became the verb English borrowed.
items.cn: liberare 意为使自由、释放，正是英语借走的那个动词。

items.en: Libertas was the abstract noun for freedom, the state that the verb produced.
items.cn: libertas 是表示「自由」的抽象名词，即那个动词所造成的状态。

items.en: Old French liberer passed the verb on, first used in legal and religious settings.
items.cn: 古法语 liberer 把这个动词传下来，最早用于法律与宗教场合。

items.en: Modern English keeps liberate for freeing peoples, prisoners, minds and substances, while liberty and liberal carry the noun and adjective side.
items.cn: 现代英语用 liberate 表示解放民族、囚犯、心灵与物质，而 liberty 与 liberal 承担名词与形容词的一面。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives on the Latin free root; the near-meaning group collects verbs of letting someone go.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「自由」词根上的同族词；近义组收表示「放人走」的动词。

entries.definition: The state of being free, the noun built beside the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 自由的状态，与动词并列构成的名词。

entries.definition: Open to new ideas or favouring individual freedom.
entries.definitionCN: 思想开放的；主张个人自由的。

entries.definition: The act of setting people free.
entries.definitionCN: 把人们释放出来的行为；解放。

entries.definition: To hand something over or to save someone, built on the same free root with a prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 送出或解救，在同一词根前加前缀构成。

entries.definition: To let someone go or to remove a limit.
entries.definitionCN: 放某人走，或去掉一项限制。

entries.definition: To let a person or thing go free.
entries.definitionCN: 放人或放物走；释放。

entries.definition: To free someone from legal or social control.
entries.definitionCN: 使摆脱法律或社会控制；解放。

entries.definition: To save someone from danger or harm.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人从危险或伤害中救出。

normalIntro.en: The word is an action made from the Latin adjective for free, and the whole family divides the work between the state, the act and the person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「自由的」形容词造出的动作，整族词把「状态、动作、人」分得清清楚楚。

normal.en: Liber is Latin for free, and the ending -are turns that adjective into the verb to make free.
normal.cn: liber 是拉丁语的「自由的」，词尾 -are 把这个形容词变成动词「使自由」。

normal.en: Liberty names the state, liberate names the act, and liberator names the person who does it.
normal.cn: liberty 指状态，liberate 指动作，liberator 指做这件事的人。

normal.en: Deliver is a prefix plus the same root: to deliver is to let something pass out of one's hands.
normal.cn: deliver 是前缀加同一词根：交出某物，就是让它离开自己的手。

normal.en: The ending -ate marks verbs of making, as in liberate and activate.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 常标记「使……发生」的动词，如 liberate 与 activate。

normal.en: Chemists say a reaction liberates a gas when the gas is set loose from a compound.
normal.cn: 化学里说某反应 liberates 一种气体，就是那种气体从化合物中被放了出来。

abstract.en: The word always has a door in it: something closed is made open.
abstract.cn: 这个词里始终有一扇门：原本关着的被打开了。

abstract.en: Freedom here is described as an action rather than a possession, which is why a verb stands beside the abstract noun.
abstract.cn: 这里的自由被说成一个动作而不是一件所有物，所以抽象名词旁边还站着一个动词。

abstract.en: To liberate a mind uses the same verb as to liberate a city, as if ideas could be held prisoner too.
abstract.cn: 解放心灵与解放城市用的是同一个动词，仿佛观念也会被关押。

examples.en: The soldiers liberated the town at dawn.
examples.cn: 士兵们在黎明时解放了这座城镇。

examples.en: The rebels liberated every prisoner in the jail.
examples.cn: 起义者把监狱里的囚犯全部释放了。

examples.en: The reaction liberates heat and light.
examples.cn: 这个反应释放出热和光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离吧，解脱了」——离吧，人一走自由就来了；liberate 是解放。

root: 拉丁语 liber（自由的）+ 动词词尾 -are，liberare 意为「使自由、释放」；同族有 liberty、liberal、liberation，前缀变体有 deliver。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person or place being let out of someone else's control; it spreads from a town to a prisoner, then to a mind, and finally to a gas inside a compound.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个人、一个地方被放出别人的控制；它从一座城扩展到一名囚犯，再扩到一颗心灵，最后扩到化合物里的气体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut padlock falling away as the gate swings outward into the light.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁锁被剪断落下，大门向光里打开。

branches.en: a gate opening for a whole crowd at dawn
branches.cn: 黎明时为一群人打开的大门

branches.en: one cell door standing open with nobody guarding it
branches.cn: 一扇没人看守的牢房门开着

branches.en: a traveller returning with a wider view of the world
branches.cn: 旅行归来、眼界变宽的旅人

branches.en: heat and light leaving a reacting mixture
branches.cn: 热与光从反应物中逸出

branches.en: one verb covering a town and a single body
branches.cn: 一个动词同时覆盖一座城与一个身体

intro.en: A Latin adjective for free, its verb, its abstract noun, and two English endings that mark action, result and person hold the family together.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「自由的」形容词、它的动词、它的抽象名词，以及两个标记动作、结果与人的英语词尾，把这个词族撑了起来。

latinIntro.en: Liber, liberare and libertas are all recorded Latin words, so the family has a reliable Latin core.
latinIntro.cn: liber、liberare 与 libertas 都是有记录的拉丁词，这一族有可靠的拉丁语内核。

definition_zh: 自由；自由权；擅自；获准行动的范围
definition_en: freedom to live and act as one chooses, especially as a condition protected by law or constitution
core_image: 一根被砸断的锁链落在石阶上，锁孔里还插着半截钥匙，人已经走远
scene: 城邦的公民在广场上宣读宪章，声称任何人不得未经审判而被拘押。Citizens in the square read out the charter declaring that no one should be detained without trial, a guarantee of personal liberty.
sceneCN: 这里指「受法律保障、不受任意拘押的个人自由」，对应第 1 个义项：法律保护的、免于任意逮捕的自由；句意为公民宣读宪章，宣布未经审判不得拘押任何人。画面要点：广场、宪章、砸断的锁链。

pos.zh: 自由；自由权（不可数；表示各项具体自由时可用复数）

collocations.zh: 获准的；自由的；有空闲的

derivatives.zh: 自由的；宽容的；自由主义的（拉丁语中表示「自由人的、宽厚的」形容词经法语传入，语义由身份转向宽宏与开明）
解放；释放（表示「自由的」词根加动词后缀，指使某人脱离束缚）
解放；释放（动词加表行为的名词后缀，指使脱离束缚的过程）
自由意志论者（表示「自由」的名词加表主张或从事者的后缀，指主张个人自由最大化的人）

senses.title: Protection from arbitrary detention
senses.titleCN: 免于任意拘押的个人自由
senses.definition: the condition of a person who cannot be arrested or held except by lawful procedure
senses.definitionCN: 除依法定程序外不得被逮捕或拘押的个人状态
senses.example: Citizens in the square read out the charter declaring that no one should be detained without trial, a guarantee of personal liberty.
senses.exampleCN: 公民在广场宣读宪章，宣布未经审判不得拘押任何人，这是对个人自由的保障。
senses.why: In Roman law the free person's body could not be seized at will, so liberty begins as a legal status rather than a mood.
senses.whyCN: 在罗马法中，自由人的身体不能被随意捉拿，因此「自由」一开始是一种法律身份，而不是一种心情。

senses.title: Self-government of a community
senses.definition: the condition of a city or people that makes its own laws instead of receiving them from a ruler
senses.definitionCN: 城市或民族自行立法、而不是从统治者那里接受法律的状态
senses.example: The city kept its liberties against the duke for two generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城邦两代人以来一直保有对抗公爵的自由权。
senses.why: Medieval towns bought charters that listed their liberties, so the word came to name a body's collective self-rule.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪城镇买下特许状，状上逐条列出它们的自由权，于是这个词也命名一个群体的自治。

senses.title: Specific rights protected by law
senses.titleCN: 法律保护的各项具体自由权
senses.definition: the several freedoms, such as speech, worship and assembly, that a constitution or statute guarantees
senses.definitionCN: 宪法或法律所保障的若干项自由，如言论、礼拜与集会
senses.example: The bill lists the liberties that the state may not remove.
senses.exampleCN: 权利法案列出了国家不得取消的各项自由。
senses.why: The abstract condition becomes countable when each guarantee is written down separately, which is why the plural is so common in legal texts.
senses.whyCN: 当每一项保障被分别写下来，抽象状态就变得可数，这就是复数形式在法律文本中如此常见的原因。

senses.title: Overstepping what is allowed
senses.definition: the act of acting beyond one's permitted scope, especially in a way that is presumptuous
senses.definitionCN: 超出自己被允许的范围行事，尤指冒失无礼地这样做
senses.example: The visitor took liberties with the archive and rearranged the files.
senses.exampleCN: 那位访客擅自摆弄档案，把文件重新排列了。
senses.why: A granted latitude can be used too far, so the same noun turns ironic and names the abuse of a permission.
senses.whyCN: 获准的余地可能被用过了头，于是同一个名词转为反讽，命名对许可的滥用。

senses.title: Being permitted or free to act
senses.definition: the state of being allowed to do something, or of being free from obligation at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 获准做某事、或在某一时刻没有义务在身的状态
senses.example: You are at liberty to inspect the records yourself.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以自行查阅这些记录。
senses.why: The phrase 'at liberty' keeps the old legal sense of a person not under restraint, and from it comes the polite formula for permission.
senses.whyCN: 「处于自由状态」这一短语保留了「人未受拘束」的旧法律义，礼貌的许可说法正是从这里来的。

senses.title: Freedom of conscience and worship
senses.definition: the right to hold and practise a faith without state pressure
senses.definitionCN: 不受国家压力地持有并实践信仰的权利
senses.example: Religious liberty was the first liberty to be argued for in print.
senses.exampleCN: 宗教自由是最早被以印刷文字论证的自由。
senses.why: Where the state and the church were the same body, the demand to worship otherwise was the sharpest test of a protected sphere.
senses.whyCN: 当国家与教会合为一体，要求以别的方式礼拜，就成了对「受保护领域」最尖锐的检验。

senses.title: Freedom of the will
senses.definition: the philosophical claim that a person can choose without being wholly determined by prior causes
senses.definitionCN: 人能够作出选择、而不完全被先在原因所决定的哲学主张
senses.example: The essay asks whether liberty of the will survives a strict causal account.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章追问，在严格的决定论解释下，意志自由是否还能成立。
senses.why: Once legal restraint is removed, the remaining question is whether anything else restrains the will, and the word follows the question inward.
senses.whyCN: 一旦法律约束被移除，剩下的问题就是是否有别的东西在约束意志，这个词便随问题向内走。

senses.title: The range of a granted freedom
senses.definition: the extent of a place or body of knowledge that a person is allowed to use
senses.definitionCN: 一个人被允许使用的场所或知识范围
senses.example: The scholar was given the liberty of the whole collection.
senses.exampleCN: 这位学者获准自由使用全部藏书。
senses.why: To have the liberty of a place is an old civic formula: not ownership, but the permitted run of it.
senses.whyCN: 「拥有某地的自由」是一个古老的市民说法：不是所有权，而是被允许在其中往来。

intro.en: Liberty comes from Latin libertas, the condition of a free person, built on liber 'free'. The deeper origin of liber is uncertain. English took the word through Old French, and its plural came to mean specific chartered privileges.
intro.cn: liberty 出自拉丁语 libertas，指自由人的身份，建立在 liber「自由的」之上。liber 的更深来源不确定。英语经古法语吸收此词，其复数后来指特许状上具体列明的特权。

items.en: Liber meant 'free, not a slave' and could also describe a person of noble or generous status. Its own origin is uncertain; a connection with a root meaning 'to grow' has been suggested but not established.
items.cn: liber 意为「自由的、非奴隶的」，也可形容出身高贵或气度宽厚的人。它本身的来源不确定；有人提出它与意为「生长」的词根相关，但未获确立。

items.en: Libertas named the condition of a free person and, in Roman public life, the status that law protected against arbitrary seizure.
items.cn: libertas 指自由人的身份；在罗马公共生活中，它指法律保护、免于任意捉拿的身份。

items.en: Old French liberte carried the noun into English, at first in religious and civic contexts rather than in philosophy.
items.cn: 古法语 liberte 把这个名词带入英语，最初用于宗教与市民语境，而不是哲学。

items.en: Towns and guilds listed their liberties in charters, and the plural became a name for specific privileges held by a body.
items.cn: 城镇与行会在特许状中逐条列出自己的自由权，其复数形式于是成为某个群体所持具体特权的名称。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the singular named a general political condition, and documents began to speak of civil liberty. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，单数形式指一般的政治状态，文书开始谈论公民自由。年代为约数。

items.en: The same noun was applied to the will, producing the long debate over liberty of the will that continues in philosophy.
items.cn: 同一个名词被用到意志上，产生了关于意志自由的长期争论，这一争论在哲学中延续至今。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin adjective or looks deceptively close to it, including one word whose Latin source is a different noun altogether; the second group gives near alternatives.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个拉丁形容词构成或与它形近得容易误认，其中还有一个词的拉丁来源是另一个名词；第二组是近义替代。

entries.definition: Generous or open-minded, and in politics favourable to reform; it began as 'of a free person' and moved toward generosity of attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 宽厚的、开明的，政治上倾向改革；它起初意为「自由人的」，后来转向态度上的宽宏。

entries.definition: To set a person or place free from control; it names the act that produces liberty rather than the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 使人或地方脱离控制；它命名产生自由的动作，而不是状态。

entries.definition: A place where books are kept; its Latin source is a word for a book or the bark used for writing, not the adjective for freedom.
entries.definitionCN: 藏书之所；它的拉丁来源是表示「书」或书写用树皮的词，而不是表示自由的形容词。

entries.definition: A published false statement that harms a reputation; it comes from a small Latin book or booklet, with no link to freedom.
entries.definitionCN: 公开发表的、损害名誉的不实陈述；它出自拉丁语中表示小册子的词，与自由无关。

entries.definition: The general condition of not being bound; it covers body, will and speech, while liberty more often names a legally protected status.
entries.definitionCN: 不受束缚的一般状态；它覆盖身体、意志与言论，而本词更常指受法律保护的身份。

entries.definition: The right of a person or region to govern itself; it stresses who makes the rules rather than what is forbidden.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或地区自行治理的权利；它强调由谁制定规则，而不是禁止什么。

entries.definition: The state of not being controlled or supported by another; it is common for nations and for self-supporting people.
entries.definitionCN: 不受他人控制或供养的状态；常用于国家与自食其力的人。

entries.definition: An official permission to do something; it is narrower than liberty because it is granted case by case and can be revoked.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的官方许可；它比自由窄，因为逐案授予且可被撤回。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin adjective for a free person, real derived words and real legal formulas, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示自由人的形容词、真实派生词与真实法律套语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The core is a legal status: a free body that cannot be seized at will.
normal.cn: 核心是一种法律身份：一具不能被随意捉拿的自由身体。

normal.en: The family runs liberal, liberate, liberation and libertarian.
normal.cn: 同族词包括宽厚的、解放、解放过程与自由意志论者。

normal.en: Medieval towns kept their liberties in written charters, which is why the plural means specific privileges.
normal.cn: 中世纪城镇把自由权写进特许状，所以复数形式指具体特权。

normal.en: The phrase at liberty means both free from restraint and free to act.
normal.cn: 「处于自由状态」这一说法既指不受拘束，也指可以行动。

normal.en: Taking liberties is the ironic side: using a permission further than it was given.
normal.cn: 「擅自」是这个词的反讽一面：把许可用得比给予的更远。

abstract.en: Picture a broken chain on a step with the key still in the lock, and the person already out of sight.
abstract.cn: 想象石阶上一根断链，钥匙还插在锁里，人已经走远。

abstract.en: Picture a charter rolled open on a town table, each paragraph a named freedom.
abstract.cn: 想象城镇桌上一卷摊开的特许状，每一段都是一项有名字的自由。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked permission that opens only when the right name is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇标着「许可」的门，只有说出正确的名分才会打开。

examples.en: The court held that the detention violated his liberty.
examples.cn: 法院认定这次拘押侵犯了他的自由。

examples.en: You are at liberty to leave whenever you wish.
examples.cn: 你随时都可以离开。

examples.en: The reporter took liberties with the quotation and changed its sense.
examples.cn: 那名记者擅自改动引文，改变了它的意思。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离不体」——身体离开束缚，就不必再贴着锁链过日子；自由就是能走开的那一步。

root: 拉丁语 liber「自由的、非奴隶的」→ libertas「自由人的身份」→ 经古法语 liberte 进入英语。liber 的更深来源不确定，与意为「生长」的词根相关的说法属假说；同族的 liberalis 意为「自由人的、宽厚的」，是另一条语义支线。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings start from a free body that the law may not seize. From that status come self-rule for a community, the list of named guarantees, the permission formula, the ironic overstepping of permission, the freedom of worship, the philosophical liberty of the will, and the old civic right to move through a place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一具法律不得随意捉拿的自由身体开始。从这个身份分出共同体的自治、逐条列名的保障、许可的说法、对许可的反讽式越界、信仰的自由、哲学上的意志自由，以及古老的、可在某地往来的市民权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain broken at the link, with the key still turning in the lock.
core.cn: 核心意象：链环被砸断的锁链，钥匙还在锁里转动。

branches.en: UNBOUND BODY: protection from arbitrary arrest, and the polite formula that a person is free to act.
branches.cn: 不受束缚的身体：免于任意逮捕，以及「可以自由行动」的礼貌说法。

branches.en: SELF-RULE: a town or people that makes its own law.
branches.cn: 自治：自行立法的城镇或民族。

branches.en: NAMED GUARANTEES: the several liberties written in a charter, and the permitted run of a place.
branches.cn: 列名的保障：写进特许状的各项自由，以及在某地获准走动的范围。

branches.en: OVERSTEPPING: the same permission used beyond what was granted.
branches.cn: 越界：同一份许可被用得超出所给予的范围。

branches.en: CONSCIENCE AND WILL: worship without pressure, and the inner question of whether the will is determined.
branches.cn: 良心与意志：不受压力的礼拜，以及意志是否被决定的内在问题。

intro.en: The whole family rests on one Latin adjective for a free person, with noun, verb and agent endings added over time; the Germanic near synonym freedom belongs to a separate history.
intro.cn: 整个家族都依托一个表示自由人的拉丁形容词，随后加上名词、动词与施事后缀；日耳曼语的近义词「自由」属于另一段历史。

senses.title: A person who works in a library
senses.definition: someone whose job is to work in a library, arranging books and helping people who come to read or borrow
senses.definitionCN: 在图书馆工作、整理书籍并帮助前来阅读或借书的人
senses.example: The librarian stamped the due date on the last book.
senses.exampleCN: 那位馆员在最后一本书上盖了到期日。
senses.why: Latin librarius meant of books and also a bookseller; adding -an makes a person connected with books, so the librarian is the one whose work is tied to the collection.

senses.title: The person in charge of a library
senses.definition: the head of a library, responsible for its budget, staff and collection

senses.example: As chief librarian, she decides which journals the college buys.
senses.exampleCN: 作为馆长，她决定学院购买哪些期刊。
senses.why: The title does not split between workers and the head: responsibility for the collection is still bookkeeping, so the same word covers the person in charge.
senses.whyCN: 这个称谓并不在普通职员与负责人之间切开：对藏书的负责仍然是一种管书的事，所以同一个词也覆盖负责人。

senses.title: A specialist trained in organizing information
senses.definition: a trained professional who organizes, catalogues and searches information for users

senses.example: A law librarian can find a case in minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 法律图书馆的信息馆员几分钟就能找到一个判例。
senses.why: As collections moved from paper to databases, the same title widened to cover the skills of cataloguing and searching, not only the handling of books.
senses.whyCN: 当藏书从纸张转向数据库，同一个称谓扩展到编目与检索的本领，不再只管搬书。

intro.en: Librarian grows out of the Latin word for book, through the Latin names for a bookseller and a place of books, and is completed by an English suffix for a person.
intro.cn: librarian 从拉丁语中表示「书」的词长出来，途经拉丁语里「书商」与「藏书之处」两个名字，最后由一个英语中指人的后缀收尾。

items.en: Liber first meant the inner bark of a tree, and because people wrote on that bark it came to mean a book.
items.cn: liber 最初指树的内皮，因为人们在这层皮上写字，它后来就指书。

items.en: Librarius meant belonging to books, and as a noun it named a bookseller or a copyist.
items.cn: librarius 意为与书有关的，作名词时指书商或抄写员。

items.en: Librarium was a place for books, the ancestor of the English word for a library.
items.cn: librarium 是存放书的地方，是英语中「图书馆」一词的祖先。

items.en: Library enters English through Old French librairie, at first naming a place or a collection of books.
items.cn: library 经古法语 librairie 进入英语，最初指藏书的地方或一批藏书。

items.en: Librarian is formed inside English by adding -an to library, and is recorded from the early eighteenth century.
items.cn: librarian 是在英语内部给 library 加 -an 造出来的，最早记录见于十八世纪初。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin book root and its English offspring; the near-meaning group gathers people who care for collections.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语「书」的词根及其英语后代展开；近义组收照管藏书的人。

normalIntro.en: A Latin word for book plus an English ending for a person gives this job its name, and the family keeps the book at its centre.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「书」加一个英语中指人的词尾，给了这份职业名字，整族词始终把书放在中心。

normal.en: Liber is Latin for book, so library and librarian share one root.
normal.cn: liber 是拉丁语的「书」，所以 library 与 librarian 共用一个词根。

normal.en: The suffix -an marks a person connected with a place or a subject, as in librarian and historian.
normal.cn: 后缀 -an 标记与某个地方或学科有关的人，如 librarian 与 historian。

normal.en: Librarianship adds -ship, the ending for a job, a skill or an office.
normal.cn: librarianship 加的是 -ship，这个后缀表示职位、技能或职务。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable: li-BRAR-i-an.
normal.cn: 重音落在第二个音节：li-BRAR-i-an。

normal.en: One title covers both the head of the library and the person at the desk.
normal.cn: 一个称谓同时覆盖馆长和坐在借书台前的人。

abstract.en: A word for a keeper of books reminds us that knowledge needs shelves as much as minds.
abstract.cn: 一个「看管书的人」的词提醒人：知识既需要头脑，也同样需要书架。

abstract.en: The same root gives library and libretto, a small book that holds the words of an opera.
abstract.cn: 同一词根给出 library 与 libretto，后者是装着歌剧歌词的小书。

abstract.en: A librarian is a bridge between a stored collection and a person who needs one page of it.
abstract.cn: 馆员是藏书与那个只需要其中一页的人之间的一座桥。

examples.en: A law librarian can find a case in minutes.

definition_en: an official document that allows an activity, formal permission to do something, or the freedom to behave beyond the usual limits

senses.title: An official document that allows an activity
senses.definition: a document issued by an authority that gives a person or a business the right to do something
senses.definitionCN: 由主管机关发放、赋予个人或企业做某事的权利的证件
senses.example: He showed his driving licence to the officer.
senses.exampleCN: 他把驾驶执照出示给警官。
senses.why: Latin licentia named permission, and a licence is that permission made visible as paper, so the abstract right and the card in a wallet are the same sense at two stages.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 licentia 指的就是许可，而 licence 是把那份许可变成看得见的纸；因此抽象的权利与钱包里的卡片，是同一个义项的两个阶段。

senses.title: Formal permission to do something
senses.definition: official or formal permission, whether or not it comes with a document
senses.definitionCN: 正式或官方的准许，无论是否附有证件
senses.example: The film was shown under licence from the studio.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影获得制片公司许可后才放映。
senses.why: Strip away the paper and what remains is the permission itself; the word then names the granting rather than the certificate.
senses.whyCN: 把纸去掉，剩下的就是许可本身；此时这个词指的是「准许」这件行为，而不是那张证书。

senses.title: Freedom to behave beyond the usual limits
senses.definition: the freedom to act without restraint, often used when the freedom has gone too far
senses.definitionCN: 不受约束地行事的自由，常用于指这种自由已经过了头
senses.example: The novel's licence with facts annoyed historians.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说对史实的随意处理让历史学家不满。
senses.why: Permission with no one setting its edges turns into boldness; the same noun slides from an allowed act to an excess that others resent.
senses.whyCN: 一旦没有人给许可划边界，准许就变成大胆妄为；同一个名词从「被允许的行为」滑向「让别人不满的过头」。

senses.title: Special freedom granted to an artist or writer
senses.definition: the accepted freedom of a writer or artist to change facts or break rules for effect
senses.definitionCN: 作家或艺术家为效果而改动事实、打破常规时被认可的自由
senses.example: Poetic licence let the songwriter bend the grammar.
senses.exampleCN: 诗歌的特许自由让这位词作者改动了语法。
senses.why: The narrowest sense is a professional allowance: art is permitted to depart from fact, and the word keeps the same frame of granted freedom.
senses.whyCN: 最窄的义项是一种职业上的照顾：艺术被允许偏离事实，而这个词仍然保留「被授予的自由」这一框架。

intro.en: Licence comes from a Latin verb for being allowed, through its abstract noun, and the noun arrived in English by way of French with the sense of leave or permission.
intro.cn: licence 来自拉丁语中表示「被允许」的动词，经它的抽象名词，再由法语以「准许、许可」的意思进入英语。

items.en: Licere meant to be allowed or to be permitted, and it described what a person might lawfully do.
items.cn: licere 意为被允许、获准，描述一个人可以合法地做什么。

items.en: Licentia was the noun for freedom or permission, and it could also name boldness that oversteps.
items.cn: licentia 是表示自由或许可的名词，也可以指越界的大胆。

items.en: Old French took the noun as licence, meaning leave or permission, and handed it to English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词作 licence，意为准许或许可，并传给了英语。

items.en: Middle English licence covers a granted privilege, a formal permission and the freedom of behaviour.
items.cn: 中古英语的 licence 覆盖被授予的特权、正式的许可，以及行为上的自由。

items.en: Modern English keeps licence as the British noun and license as the American spelling, while the verb is license everywhere.
items.cn: 现代英语保留英式名词 licence 与美式拼写 license，而动词在各地都写作 license。

normalIntro.en: A Latin verb for being allowed supplies the stem, its noun adds the idea of freedom, and English splits the spelling between the noun and the verb.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「被允许」的动词提供词干，它的名词加上「自由」的含义，英语又在名词与动词之间分出拼写。

normal.en: Licere is Latin for to be allowed, and licentia is the permission that it grants.
normal.cn: licere 是拉丁语的「被允许」，licentia 是它给出的许可。

normal.en: British English keeps licence for the noun and license for the verb; American English uses license for both.
normal.cn: 英式英语名词用 licence、动词用 license；美式英语两者都用 license。

normal.en: The c sounds like an s, and the ending rhymes with fence.
normal.cn: 其中的 c 读作 s，词尾与 fence 押韵。

normal.en: The -ee in licensee marks the receiver, while the giver is the licensor.
normal.cn: licensee 里的 -ee 标记接受者，给出许可的一方则是 licensor。

normal.en: Poetic licence is a fixed phrase for the freedom to break rules in art.
normal.cn: poetic licence 是固定说法，指艺术中打破规则的自由。

abstract.en: A licence is permission turned into paper, so a right can be carried in a pocket.
abstract.cn: 执照是把许可变成纸，于是一项权利可以被装进口袋。

abstract.en: The same noun covers a permit and an excess of freedom, because both begin from permission.
abstract.cn: 同一个名词既指许可证，也指过度的自由，因为两者都从「许可」出发。

abstract.en: Every licence draws a line: it says what may be done and quietly says what may not.
abstract.cn: 每一张执照都划出一条线：它写明可以做什么，也悄悄写明不可以做什么。
